issues.title: repo: add an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 manifest (root plugin.json + mcp.json) so Cursor and Codex load vn-skills as a plugin
issues.body:
## Problem

Agent Plugins 1.0.0 (https://agent-plugins.org) is a vendor-neutral plugin format. Its steering committee includes Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI and Vercel. Cursor's docs say plugins that follow the spec load in Cursor (https://cursor.com/docs/plugins). OpenAI's docs say a root `plugin.json` is now the preferred manifest for ChatGPT/Codex plugins, with `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` kept as a fallback (https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins).

vn-skills ships only the Claude Code plugin files: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and an unversioned `.mcp.json`. There is no root `plugin.json` and no root `mcp.json`. The skills are already where the spec expects them (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`), so only the two manifests are missing.

What the spec requires (from https://agent-plugins.org/plugin-authors/build-an-agent-plugin and https://agent-plugins.org/plugin-authors/mcp-servers):

- `plugin.json` at the repo root with `"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json"`, a kebab-case `name`, `version` and `description`. Skills under `skills/` need no manifest field.
- `mcp.json` at the repo root with `"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json"` and only an `mcpServers` object. Each server needs `"type": "stdio"` and `command` as a single executable token.

## What to add

`plugin.json`:
- `name`: `vn-skills`
- `version`: the current root `package.json` version
- `description`: reuse the text from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
- `license`, `homepage` and `repository`: same values as `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, only where the schema allows these fields

`mcp.json`:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json",
  "mcpServers": {
    "vn-skills": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp@<exact version>"] }
  }
}
```

## Version sync

Both version fields must move with each release. Add `plugin.json` `$.version` to `extra-files` in `release-please-config.json`; the existing `json` updater handles that. The pinned `@vn-skills/mcp@<version>` string in `mcp.json` has the same sync problem as `.mcp.json` in #154. Use whatever mechanism #154 adopts, so both files are updated the same way. Do this after #154 is merged, or in the same PR if the maintainer agrees.

This issue explicitly allows the `release-please-config.json` change.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` exist with the fields above and end with a newline
- [ ] `tests/plugin.test.ts` gains tests checking:
  - [ ] `plugin.json` has the 1.0.0 schema URL, `name === 'vn-skills'`, and `version` equal to root `package.json` `version`
  - [ ] `mcp.json` has only `$schema` and `mcpServers`, the server has `type: 'stdio'` and `command: 'npx'`, and its args pin `@vn-skills/mcp@` to the version in `packages/mcp/package.json`
- [ ] `release-please-config.json` updates `plugin.json` `$.version`, and `mcp.json`'s pin uses the same mechanism as #154
- [ ] `.claude-plugin/*` and `.mcp.json` are unchanged by this PR, apart from any change #154 makes to them
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: one short line under "Install the skills" saying the repo is also an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 plugin (Cursor/Codex), with a link to agent-plugins.org
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: The project has 0 stars but about 2k monthly npm downloads, so the reach comes from install channels, not GitHub discovery. One standard manifest makes the existing skills + MCP server installable as a plugin in Cursor and Codex, and is a prerequisite for their plugin directories.
issues.skip_reason: coder gave up: Added root plugin.json and mcp.json (pinned @vn-skills/mcp@0.6.0) and the README.md/README.vi.md lines. The issue also requires a release-please-config.json extra-files entry for plugin.json $.version, and tests/plugin.test.ts asserts it, but the CI gate rejects any change to that file. I reverted my edit to it. A maintainer must add the entry or allow the path. The #154 mechanism for the mcp.json pin is not handled, and I did not run the build, lint or tests.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
CI gate failed: touches forbidden path release-please-config.json
issues.summary: Added root plugin.json and mcp.json (Agent Plugins 1.0.0), release-please extra-file for plugin.json $.version, and README/README.vi lines. mcp.json pin sync deferred to #154's mechanism (not yet present).
issues.repro_notes: Added 'Agent Plugins 1.0.0 manifests' describe block. Fails because root plugin.json and mcp.json do not exist and release-please-config.json has no plugin.json extra-file entry.

issues.title: docs: say that GitHub Copilot loads skills from .agents/skills and .claude/skills
issues.body:
## Problem
GitHub's and VS Code's docs (read 2026-10-24) say Agent Skills work in Copilot: VS Code agent mode, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Copilot CLI, Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review.

- Copilot loads project skills from `.github/skills`, `.claude/skills` or `.agents/skills`.
- It loads personal skills from `~/.copilot/skills` or `~/.agents/skills`.
- Personal skills are not available to the cloud agent.

Sources:
- https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/customizations/agent-skills
- https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills
- https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/customize-cloud-agent/add-skills

So `vn-skills install all --agent agents` and `--agent claude` already work for Copilot users. Our docs never say so. These four places list Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI as readers of `.agents/skills/`, and Copilot is not mentioned anywhere in the repo:

- `README.md:75`
- `README.vi.md:73`
- `docs/quickstart.md:121`
- `docs/quickstart.vi.md:121`

## Acceptance
- [ ] `README.md` and `docs/quickstart.md`: add GitHub Copilot (VS Code, Copilot CLI, cloud agent) to the list of agents that read `.agents/skills/`. Link https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/customizations/agent-skills.
- [ ] Same change in Vietnamese in `README.vi.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md`.
- [ ] Add one sentence to all four files: for the Copilot cloud agent, install in project scope (`--agent agents` without `--global`), because the cloud agent does not load personal skills.
- [ ] No code changes. `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes, and `pnpm format:check` passes.
issues.triage_reason: Copilot is probably the agent with the most users, and our install paths already work for it. Saying so in the README costs one line, and with 0 stars and about 700 npm downloads a month, reach is what moves adoption now.
issues.summary: Added GitHub Copilot (VS Code, Copilot CLI, cloud agent) with docs link to the .agents/skills reader list, plus a project-scope note for the cloud agent, in README.md, README.vi.md, docs/quickstart.md and docs/quickstart.vi.md.

issues.title: vn-lunar: return INVALID_TIMEZONE instead of ok:true with day:null for a non-numeric timeZone
issues.body:
## Problem
These exported functions take a public `timeZone` parameter (default `VN_TIMEZONE`) and never validate it:

- `lunarInfo` (`packages/core/src/lunar/index.ts:54-59`)
- `solarToLunar` (`packages/core/src/lunar/convert.ts:122-126`)
- `lunarToSolar` (`convert.ts:181-186`)

A string such as `'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'`, `NaN` or `Infinity` turns the new-moon arithmetic into NaN, but the result still says success:

```
lunarInfo(10, 2, 2024, 'x' as any)
→ {"ok":true,"day":null,"month":1,"year":2024,...,"yearCanChi":"Giáp Thìn",...}
```

Every other core module returns `{ ok: false, error }` for bad input. Only library callers are affected: the CLI and MCP tools do not expose a timezone option.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `solarToLunar`, `lunarToSolar` and `lunarInfo` return `fail('INVALID_TIMEZONE', …)` with a `hint` when `timeZone` is not a finite number in the UTC offset range -12 to +14 (hours). The hint should say the value is a UTC offset in hours, e.g. `7` for Vietnam.
- [ ] `leapMonthOf` and `lunarMonthLength`, which return `number | null`, return `null` for an invalid `timeZone` instead of computing with NaN.
- [ ] Omitting `timeZone`, or passing `VN_TIMEZONE` or `7`, gives exactly the same results as today. All existing tests and `tests/golden/vn-lunar.json` still pass.
- [ ] New tests in `tests/lunar.test.ts` cover a string, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-13`, `15`, a valid non-VN offset (`8`), and `lunarToSolar` with a bad timeZone.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` passes.
issues.triage_reason: A library call that silently returns `ok:true` with `day:null` breaks the documented contract that bad input gets an `ok:false` result, and callers that trust `ok` will use a wrong date. The fix is small and local.
issues.summary: Added timeZone validation (finite number in [-12,14]) to solarToLunar/lunarToSolar (INVALID_TIMEZONE with UTC-offset hint; lunarInfo inherits it) and made leapMonthOf/lunarMonthLength return null for invalid timeZone.

issues.title: vietqr: find the CRC tag by position so a payload whose CRC is 6304 parses as valid
issues.body:
## Problem
`parseVietQR` locates the CRC field with `payload.lastIndexOf('6304')` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/parse.ts:46`). When the 4-hex-digit CRC value is itself `6304`, the last match is the CRC value, not the tag header. The CRC is then computed over the wrong prefix, so `crcValid` is `false` and a bogus warning is added. This affects about 1 in 65,536 payloads, including ones `buildVietQR` produced itself, so build → parse does not round-trip. Callers that gate on `crcValid` reject a correct code.

Reproduction (amount found by looping `buildVietQR({bank:'VCB',account:'123',amount:i})` until `crc === '6304'`):

```
buildVietQR({ bank: 'VCB', account: '123', amount: 148444 }).payload
// 00020101021238470010A0000007270117000697043601031230208QRIBFTTA530370454061484445802VN63046304
parseVietQR(payload)
// crcValid: false, warnings: ['CRC mismatch: payload has 6304, expected FA09.']
```

The lower-case detection branch just below (lines 50-58) uses the same `crcIndex` and has the same flaw.

## Fix
Take the CRC position from the structure, not a substring search. For example, when the last top-level TLV node is tag `63` with length `04`, the tag header starts at `payload.length - 8`. Check `payload.slice(-8, -4).toUpperCase() === '6304'` and hash `payload.slice(0, payload.length - 4)`. Keep the existing behaviour for payloads where tag 63 is missing or not last (the `CRC tag 63 is not the last field.` warning).

## Acceptance
- [ ] `parseVietQR` of the amount-148444 payload above returns `ok: true`, `crcValid: true` and no CRC warning
- [ ] Golden case added to `tests/golden/vietqr.json` for that payload (pure input → output)
- [ ] A test that builds the amount-148444 payload with `buildVietQR` and checks the parse round-trips
- [ ] The lower-cased-payload warning (#131 behaviour) still works, including for a lower-cased payload whose CRC is `6304`
- [ ] Existing vietqr tests pass; `pnpm format` and `pnpm lint` clean
issues.triage_reason: This is a correctness bug in the flagship skill: the toolkit rejects its own valid output, which undermines its main promise of validating payloads. The fix is small and the test case is already known.
issues.summary: parseVietQR now locates the CRC header by position (payload.length - 8) when tag 63 is last and its header reads 6304, falling back to lastIndexOf otherwise, so payloads whose CRC value is 6304 validate correctly; the lower-case detection branch uses the same index.

issues.title: cli: make `address convert-file` errors honour --json with READ_ERROR / COLUMN_NOT_FOUND codes
issues.body:
## Problem
`vn-skills address convert-file` uses a local `fail()` helper (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts:156-159`) that always writes `Error: ...` to stderr as plain text, even with `--json`. Every other command returns `{ok:false,error:{code,message,hint}}` through `failExit` (`packages/cli/src/output.ts:23`). Examples are `vietqr decode` (`READ_ERROR` in `packages/cli/src/decode.ts`) and `einvoice validate` (`READ_ERROR` in `packages/cli/src/commands/einvoice.ts`). Agents that parse stdout get nothing.

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json address convert-file nofile
Error: cannot read nofile: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'nofile'   (exit 1)
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json address convert-file tmp.csv --csv --column nope
Error: column "nope" not found in CSV header (name, address)   (exit 1)
```

Three paths are affected: `--csv` without `--column` (line 160), an unreadable file (line 168) and an unknown column (line 176).

## Fix
Replace the local `fail` with `failExit(c, {code, message, hint})`. Add the `Command` argument to the `.action` callback, as the other subcommands do. Suggested codes: `MISSING_COLUMN` (`--csv` without `--column`), `READ_ERROR` (file cannot be read), `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND` (header lacks the column; the hint lists the available columns). Keep exit code 1 for these, and exit code 2 for "some rows failed".

## Acceptance
- [ ] With `--json`, all three cases print the `{ok:false,error:{code,message,hint}}` JSON on stdout and exit 1
- [ ] Without `--json` on a TTY, they print `Error [CODE]: ...` and `Hint: ...` like other commands
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` for each of the three cases (use a temp dir for the CSV)
- [ ] Exit code 2 for partial row failures is unchanged
- [ ] `pnpm format` and `pnpm lint` clean
issues.triage_reason: `convert-file` is the newest command and covers the main address job: bulk-migrating old addresses. Agents depend on the JSON error shape, and this command is the only one that breaks it.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
The coder found the regression test wrong (rewrite it):
Implemented failExit with MISSING_COLUMN/READ_ERROR/COLUMN_NOT_FOUND in address convert-file (59/60 tests pass, including the new --json tests). The remaining failure is the old test '--csv without --column fails' (tests/cli.test.ts:382), which asserts r.err contains 'column' with no --json and piped stdout; failExit correctly emits JSON on stdout when stdout is not a TTY, so stderr is empty. The test should check `${r.out}${r.err}`.
issues.summary: Replaced local fail() in address convert-file with failExit (MISSING_COLUMN, READ_ERROR, COLUMN_NOT_FOUND with hints); added Command arg to action. Exit codes unchanged.

issues.title: mcp: add a Dockerfile that runs the stdio MCP server, as needed for the Docker MCP Catalog
issues.body:
## Problem
Docker's MCP registry (`docker/mcp-registry`) feeds hub.docker.com/mcp and Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit. Its CONTRIBUTING.md (read 2026-10-24) says local (stdio) servers need a Dockerfile in the source repo. The submission tooling builds that image, runs it and checks that it lists tools. vn-skills has no `Dockerfile` or `.dockerignore`, so it cannot be submitted. The server is offline and needs no secrets or env config, which keeps the image simple.

## What to build
- A root `Dockerfile` that builds `@vn-skills/mcp` from this workspace, so the version always matches the commit Docker pins and no release-sync step is needed:
  - Node 22 base image (an `-alpine` or `-slim` variant is fine)
  - `corepack enable`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build`, then a slim runtime stage with only what `packages/mcp/dist/index.js` needs at runtime (core `dist` + `data`, prod deps)
  - Run as a non-root user
  - `ENTRYPOINT ["node", "packages/mcp/dist/index.js"]` (or the equivalent path in the runtime stage), stdio transport, no exposed ports
- A root `.dockerignore` that excludes `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist` build outputs, tests and docs not needed for the build
- A short "Docker" subsection under "MCP client setup" in `README.md` and `README.vi.md`: `docker build -t vn-skills-mcp .` plus a client config using `docker run -i --rm vn-skills-mcp`

Do not change `.github/workflows/` or release config in this issue.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `docker build -t vn-skills-mcp .` succeeds from a clean checkout
- [ ] Sending `initialize` then `tools/list` JSON-RPC lines to `docker run -i --rm vn-skills-mcp` returns the 28 tools (state in the PR if Docker was not available to run this)
- [ ] The container makes no network calls at runtime and needs no env vars
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md updated in both languages; files end with a newline
- [ ] `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm lint` clean
issues.triage_reason: npm downloads (858/month for the MCP server) are the only traction signal, and they come from MCP users. Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit is a large MCP channel where vn-skills is absent, and a Dockerfile is the only missing prerequisite.

issues.title: cli: reject install --agent values that are Object.prototype keys with the Unknown agent error
issues.body:
## Problem

`packages/cli/src/commands/install.ts` stores the agent folders in an ordinary object literal (`const AGENT_DIRS: Record<string, string> = { claude: '.claude', ... }`, lines 7-13). The `install` action looks up `AGENT_DIRS[o.agent]` and only checks that the result is truthy (`if (!agentDir) throw new Error('Unknown agent ...')`).

For agent names that are inherited `Object.prototype` keys (`constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__`, ...), the lookup returns a function or `Object.prototype`, which is truthy. The check is skipped, and the command then fails inside `path.join` with an error that never mentions the agent:

```text
$ cd /tmp && node <repo>/packages/cli/dist/index.js install all --agent constructor --dry-run
The "path" argument must be of type string. Received function Object
```

The intended message, `Unknown agent "constructor". Use one of: claude, cursor, codex, agents, copilot`, is never shown. `tests/cli.test.ts` only covers an invalid agent named `nope` (around line 538).

## Fix

Look the agent up only among its own keys, for example `Object.hasOwn(AGENT_DIRS, o.agent) ? AGENT_DIRS[o.agent] : undefined`, or turn `AGENT_DIRS` into a `Map`. Do the same for any other lookup in this file that indexes `AGENT_DIRS` with user input, including the special case that maps `copilot` to `.github` in project scope. The list of valid agents and their target folders stays the same.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `install vietqr --agent constructor`, `--agent toString`, `--agent hasOwnProperty` and `--agent __proto__` exit non-zero and print `Unknown agent "<name>". Use one of: claude, cursor, codex, agents, copilot` on stderr. With `--dry-run` they also write nothing.
- [ ] New cases in `tests/cli.test.ts` next to the existing unknown-agent test cover these names. They fail on the current code.
- [ ] The existing install tests for claude, cursor, codex, agents and copilot still pass.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
issues.triage_reason: `install` is the main way people adopt the skills. A crash that doesn't name the bad agent is a confusing first experience, and the fix is a single line.
issues.summary: Agent lookup in install.ts now uses Object.hasOwn so prototype keys like constructor/toString/__proto__ hit the Unknown agent error.

issues.body:
## Problem

Cline's MCP Marketplace (https://github.com/cline/mcp-marketplace) asks submitters to confirm that Cline can install the server by itself, using `README.md` or an optional `llms-install.md` at the repo root. The repo has no `llms-install.md`. The MCP setup in `README.md` is mixed in with skills, the CLI and other clients, so it is harder for an agent to follow than one short, MCP-only guide.

The server needs no API keys or env vars and runs over stdio with `npx -y @vn-skills/mcp` (Node.js 22+). The repo already documents all of this in README.md under "MCP server" and "MCP client setup".

## What to add

A root `llms-install.md`, in English, written for an AI agent that is installing the MCP server. Copy the facts from `README.md`; do not add new ones.

- Requirements: Node.js 22+, no accounts, API keys or env vars; the server is offline.
- The `mcpServers` config block exactly as in README.md: `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`. - The Docker alternative from README.md (`docker build -t vn-skills-mcp .` then `docker run -i --rm vn-skills-mcp`).
- A one-line note that it is an offline toolkit, not a payment gateway (same wording as the README).

issues.title: vn-address: convert many addresses in one call (core function + vn_address_convert_batch MCP tool)
issues.body:
## Problem

Bulk conversion of old 63-province addresses is the main job for the address skill, and competing npm packages advertise CSV migration (see #156). vn-skills now has `vn-skills address convert-file` (#161), but that logic lives only in the CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts`, the `convert-file <file>` command). Nothing is exported from `@vn-skills/core`, and there is no MCP tool for it.

The MCP tool `vn_address_convert` (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`, around line 200) takes one address per call. An agent working through MCP on a customer list therefore has to make one tool call per row. That is slow, uses a lot of context, and the agent has no summary of which rows failed. `@vn-skills/mcp` is the most-downloaded package (858 a month), so this gap affects the main way people use vn-skills.

This needs no new data or Vietnamese facts. It reuses `convertAddress` and the existing mapping.

## Proposal

1. **Core.** Add `convertAddresses(inputs)` in `packages/core/src/address/` and export it from `packages/core/src/index.ts`.
   - `inputs` is an array of free-text address strings.
   - It returns `{ ok: true, results, summary: { total, converted, failed } }`.
   - `results[i]` holds `index`, `input` and either the same fields `convert-file` emits per row or `{ ok: false, error }`.
   - It never throws for null, non-string or empty items; each such item becomes a per-row error.
   - A non-array argument returns a top-level `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_INPUT', ... } }`.
   - More than 1000 items returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'TOO_MANY', message, hint } }`. The hint points to `vn-skills address convert-file` for larger inputs.
2. **CLI.** Change `address convert-file` to call `convertAddresses` per chunk (or row), so the CLI and MCP share one code path. The NDJSON/CSV output and the exit code (2 when some rows fail) must stay exactly the same as today.
3. **MCP.** Add `vn_address_convert_batch` to `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` with input `{ addresses: string[] }` (zod array of strings, max 1000). It returns the core result as JSON. Describe it like `vn_address_convert` and name the 1000 limit.
4. **Docs.**
   - Add the tool to the `vn-address` row of the MCP tools table in `README.md` and `README.vi.md`, and change the tool count from 28 to 29.
   - Mention the batch tool in `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md`.
   - Update the MCP Registry description only if it lists tools (it should not need to change).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `convertAddresses` is exported from `@vn-skills/core`. Tests cover: a mixed batch with one row that converts and one unknown address, plus null, `''` and a number. Also an empty array (`total: 0`), 1001 items (`TOO_MANY`) and a non-array argument.
- [ ] For a sample batch, results match calling `convertAddress` on each item.
- [ ] Existing `address convert-file` tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` pass unchanged (same output and exit codes).
- [ ] `tests/mcp.test.ts` lists `vn_address_convert_batch` and calls it with 2 addresses, checking `summary.converted`/`summary.failed`.
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md list the new tool and say 29 tools. `tests/readme.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
issues.triage_reason: MCP is the most-downloaded package, and bulk 63→34 address migration is what address users come for. Right now an MCP agent must make one call per row. This reuses existing data and needs no new facts.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- The test 'matches convertAddress per item' only compares `mappingType` for one item. The issue requires that results match calling `convertAddress` on each item. It should compare the full row fields (old, new, candidates, confidence, warnings) over a multi-item sample batch.
- The doc comment on `conversionFields` says it is shared by 'the MCP tools'. The existing `vn_address_convert` tool does not use it, so the comment is untrue. Fix the comment or actually share the code.
- `conversionFields` and `MAX_BATCH_ADDRESSES` are newly exported from the address index and so become public `@vn-skills/core` API, which the issue did not ask for. Keep them internal, or use only `convertAddresses` and its types.

Tests cover the mixed batch, an empty array, 1001 items, a non-array argument, a full-field comparison with convertAddress, and the MCP tool. Review feedback addressed.

issues.title: vietqr: check the 13-digit amount limit on the digit string, not on Number(amount)
issues.body:
## Problem

`buildVietQR` converts the amount with `Number(raw)` and then checks `String(amount).length > 13` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:95-97`). For 21 or more digits, `String(Number)` switches to exponent notation, so the check sees a short string:

```
buildVietQR({ bank: 'VCB', account: '123', amount: '9'.repeat(30) })
→ ok: true, payload ...54051e+305802VN6304 6F5A, amount 1e+30
```

Tag 54 is set to `1e+30`, which is not a valid EMVCo amount. `parseVietQR` on that payload also returns `ok: true` with a matching CRC, so a broken QR code gets through both steps. Amounts above 2^53 that are 14–20 digits long are already rejected by the length check, but the precision loss is a second reason to check before converting: `12345678901234567890` becomes `12345678901234567000`.

## Fix

Work on the digit string `raw` that `parseAmountString` returns:
- strip leading zeros
- reject an empty or all-zero result with the existing `Amount must be greater than 0` error
- reject more than 13 digits with the existing `INVALID_AMOUNT` / `Amount exceeds 13 digits allowed by EMVCo` error
- only then build the tag value. Use the stripped digit string so the payload never contains exponent notation.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `buildVietQR({bank:'VCB',account:'123',amount:'9'.repeat(30)})` returns `ok:false` with code `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] `amount: '12345678901234567890'` (20 digits) returns `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] `amount: '9999999999999'` (13 digits) still builds, and tag 54 is exactly `9999999999999`
- [ ] `amount: '00500000'` builds with tag 54 = `500000`
- [ ] Golden cases for the 30-digit and 13-digit amounts are added to `tests/golden/vietqr.json` (loaded by `tests/golden.ts`)
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: The library reports a corrupt payment QR as valid at both build and parse time. That defeats the point of a validation toolkit, and the fix is a few lines.
issues.summary: buildVietQR now validates the amount on the digit string: strips leading zeros, rejects empty/zero and >13 digits with INVALID_AMOUNT, and writes tag 54 from the stripped digits (no exponent notation or precision loss). Target tests pass; build, typecheck, lint and format:check pass. tests/readme.test.ts fails on a tool-count mismatch (29 expected vs 28 in llms-install.md), which looks unrelated to this change.
issues.blocked: gate broken on base: pnpm exec vitest run
issues.repro_notes: Golden case 'rejects a 30-digit amount' fails on base: build returns ok:true with exponent-notation tag 54 (1e+30) instead of INVALID_AMOUNT. The 20-digit case is already rejected by the length check, and the 13-digit and leading-zero tests already pass, so they act as guards for the fix.

issues.title: mcp: return per-row errors for null or non-string entries in vn_address_convert_batch
issues.body:
## Problem

`vn_address_convert_batch` declares `addresses: z.array(z.string()).max(1000)` (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts:207`). A single `null` entry, for example an empty CSV cell sent as JSON, fails input validation for the whole call:

```
tools/call vn_address_convert_batch {"addresses":["Hà Nội",null,""]}
→ MCP error -32602: Input validation error: ... expected string, received null at addresses[1]
```

The caller gets no row results at all. The tool description and `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` promise results for each row plus a summary `{ total, converted, failed }`. The core function `convertAddresses(inputs: unknown)` (`packages/core/src/address/convert.ts:262`) already handles any array and returns a per-row result for each entry, so only the MCP schema gets in the way.

## Fix

Let each array entry be any value (e.g. `z.array(z.unknown()).max(1000)` or `z.array(z.string().nullable())`, whichever fits the SDK's JSON-schema output). Keep the 1000 limit. Pass the array straight to `convertAddresses` so bad entries come back as `ok:false` rows and are counted in `summary.failed`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A test in `tests/mcp.test.ts` calls the tool with `["Hà Nội", null, ""]` and gets `ok:true`, three rows, row 1 `ok:false` with an error code, and a summary with `failed >= 1`
- [ ] More than 1000 entries is still rejected
- [ ] The tool description and `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` say that null or empty entries come back as failed rows
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: The batch tool was just added (#198), and its main use, converting customer databases, regularly has missing cells. One null value should not discard the whole batch.

issues.title: cli: exit quietly when stdout is closed early in `address convert-file` (EPIPE)
issues.body:
## Problem

Piping `address convert-file` into a reader that stops early prints a Node stack trace and exits with status 1:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json address convert-file big.txt | head -c 10
node:events:497
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
Error: write EPIPE
  code: 'EPIPE', syscall: 'write'
```

The line-by-line loop (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts:219-236`) calls `process.stdout.write` for every row, and nothing handles a stdout `error` event. Previewing a large file with `| head` is a normal thing to do.

## Fix

When stdout is closed by the reader (`EPIPE`), stop writing and exit quietly with status 0, the way other Unix-style tools do. Handle this once for the CLI, e.g. a `process.stdout.on('error', …)` handler in `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, so every command is covered. Other stdout errors should still be reported on stderr with exit code 1.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A test in `tests/cli.test.ts` runs `address convert-file` on a file with several hundred lines, with stdout piped into a reader that closes after the first bytes. It asserts that stderr has no `EPIPE` stack trace and the CLI exits with 0
- [ ] Normal `convert-file` output and its exit code 2 for failed rows are unchanged
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: Bulk conversion is the newest headline CLI feature. A stack trace on `| head` is the first thing a user previewing a file sees.
issues.summary: Added a process.stdout 'error' handler in the CLI entry: EPIPE exits 0 silently; other stdout errors go to stderr with exit 1.
issues.blocked: gate broken on base: pnpm exec vitest run
issues.repro_notes: New test spawns the CLI with `--json address convert-file` on an 800-line file and destroys the reader's stdout after the first chunk. It fails on the base: stderr has the unhandled EPIPE stack trace. It should pass once EPIPE on stdout exits quietly with 0.

## Problem
`buildVietQR` removes all whitespace from the account without saying so (`packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:76`):

```ts
const account = String(opts.account ?? '').replace(/\s+/g, '');
```

A mistyped account is silently turned into a different one, and the result shows no sign of the change:

```

{"ok":true,"payload":"...0106abcdef...","account":"abcdef",...,"warnings":[]}
```

- [ ] The warning shows in `vn-skills vietqr build` JSON output and in the `vietqr_build` MCP tool result.

issues.title: cli: give `vietqr decode` clear errors for an empty path and a missing file
issues.body:
## Problem

`decodeQrPng` (`packages/cli/src/decode.ts:18-28`) wraps every read failure in one `READ_ERROR`. That error uses the raw Node message and a hint about PNG format:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json vietqr decode ""
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"READ_ERROR","message":"cannot read  as PNG: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open ''","hint":"Only PNG images are supported; convert screenshots or JPEGs to PNG first."}}
```

The message has a double space where the file name should be. It also exposes a raw `ENOENT`, and the hint points at the image format when the real problem is that no file was given (or the file doesn't exist).

## Fix

In `decodeQrPng`, handle these cases before the PNG parse:

1. Empty or blank `file` → `{ code: 'EMPTY', message: 'No image file given', hint: 'Pass the path to a PNG file, e.g. vn-skills vietqr decode qr.png.' }`
2. File missing (`ENOENT`) → `{ code: 'READ_ERROR', message: 'File "<file>" not found', hint: 'Check the path.' }`
3. Any other read or PNG-parse failure → keep the current `READ_ERROR` and the PNG hint, but quote the file name.

Keep the exit code the CLI uses today for decode errors.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `--json vietqr decode ""` prints `code: "EMPTY"` with a hint and no `ENOENT` text
- [ ] `--json vietqr decode does-not-exist.png` prints `READ_ERROR` with a message naming the file and the hint `Check the path.`
- [ ] A file that exists but is not a PNG (e.g. a text file) still gets `READ_ERROR` with the PNG hint
- [ ] Tests for all three cases in `tests/cli.test.ts` (use a temp dir)
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: When a decode fails, the error is the first thing a new user sees. Right now it sends them to fix the image format instead of the path.
issues.summary: decodeQrPng now returns EMPTY for blank path, READ_ERROR 'File "x" not found' with 'Check the path.' for ENOENT, and quotes the file name in other read/PNG errors.

issues.title: vietqr: warn when an amount with ',' separators such as '1,000' is read as thousands
issues.body:
## Problem

`parseAmountString` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:51-59`) accepts both `.` and `,` as thousands separators:

```ts
if (/^\d{1,3}([.,]\d{3})+$/.test(s)) return s.replace(/[.,]/g, '');
```

In Vietnamese number formatting `,` is the decimal mark (`1.234.567,89`; see `vn-number-format`). So `'1,5'` is rejected as `INVALID_AMOUNT`, but `'1,000'` is taken as 1000 ₫. `buildVietQR` returns `ok: true` with no warning. A user who meant a decimal gets a QR for a different amount and is not told:

```
buildVietQR({ bank: 'VCB', account: '123', amount: '1,000' })  -> ok:true, payload contains 54041000, warnings: []
buildVietQR({ bank: 'VCB', account: '123', amount: '1,5' })    -> INVALID_AMOUNT
```

No test or doc covers this.

## Fix

Keep accepting `'1,000'` so English-style input doesn't break. In `buildVietQR`, when the input amount string uses `,` as a group separator, push a warning such as `Amount "1,000" was read as 1000 VND; in Vietnamese ',' is the decimal mark. Pass plain digits to avoid ambiguity.` Leave the return value of `parseAmountString` unchanged; it is exported.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `buildVietQR({ ..., amount: '1,000' })` returns `ok: true`, `amount: 1000` and a warning that names the input and the value it was read as
- [ ] `'1,000,000'` gets the same warning; `'1.000.000'`, `'1000000'`, `'500000đ'` and number inputs get no amount warning
- [ ] `'1,5'` still returns `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] Tests in `tests/vietqr.test.ts` (and golden cases in `tests/golden/vietqr.json` if that fixture format covers warnings)
- [ ] `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md` common-mistakes section says to pass plain digits and explains the warning
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: A silently wrong amount in a payment QR is the worst kind of failure for this skill. A warning fixes it without breaking callers who use English-style separators.

- Missing golden case. A bug fix must add a pure input -> output case to tests/golden/vietqr.json. The issue explicitly asks for one when the fixture format covers warnings, and it does: the parseVietQR cases already assert a `warnings` array, and `expected` is matched with toMatchObject. Add buildVietQR cases for amount "1,000" and "1,000,000" with the exact warning text, and optionally a dot-separated case with `warnings: []`. The existing "amount with comma separators" case ("1,500,000") only asserts the amount, so it does not cover the warning.

issues.title: vn-number-format: return a distinct EMPTY error when parseAmount gets empty or blank input
issues.body:
## Problem

`parseAmount` (`packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts:140-142`) handles empty input the same way as any other input it can't parse. It returns the generic `INVALID_AMOUNT` error:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json numfmt parse ""
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_AMOUNT","message":"Cannot parse amount \"\"","hint":"Try \"1tr2\", \"500k\", \"1.200.000\""}}
```

The other parsers now return a separate code for empty input: phone and tax ID (`EMPTY`, #114, #141), citizen ID (`EMPTY`, #214/#221) and name split (`EMPTY_NAME`):

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json name split ""
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"EMPTY_NAME","message":"Name is empty","hint":"Pass a non-empty full name"}}
```

An agent that branches on the error code can't tell "nothing was given" apart from "the amount was typed wrong".

## Fix

In `parseAmount`, after `const raw = String(input ?? '')`, return `fail('EMPTY', 'Amount is empty', 'Pass a non-empty amount, e.g. "1tr2", "500k" or "1.200.000"')` when `raw.trim()` is empty. Use the same `EMPTY` code and message style as `packages/core/src/taxid` and `packages/core/src/id`. Input that is not empty but can't be parsed keeps `INVALID_AMOUNT`.

If the CLI `numfmt parse` command or the `vn_number_format` MCP tool (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`) lists or documents error codes, add `EMPTY` there too. Do the same in `skills/vn-number-format/SKILL.md` if it lists error codes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `parseAmount('')`, `parseAmount('   ')`, `parseAmount(null as any)` and `parseAmount(undefined as any)` return `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'EMPTY', message, hint } }`, and `hint` is not empty
- [ ] `parseAmount('abc')` still returns `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] Golden cases for `""` and `"   "` → `EMPTY` added to `tests/golden/vn-number-format.json`, following the existing case format
- [ ] A CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts`: `--json numfmt parse ""` prints `code: "EMPTY"`
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: This is the last parser that still sends empty input to a generic error code. Phone, tax ID, ID and name were all fixed in the last few days, so this completes that work.

issues.title: vn-einvoice: return an error instead of throwing when computeTotals gets null, a non-object or no lines array
issues.body:
## Problem
`computeTotals` (`packages/core/src/einvoice/totals.ts:40-50`) loops over `invoice.lines` without checking its argument. A null invoice, a string, or an object without a `lines` array throws a `TypeError`:

```
computeTotals(null)  -> THROW Cannot read properties of null (reading 'lines')
```

`validateInvoice` in the same module (`packages/core/src/einvoice/schema.ts:134`) handles the same input and returns `{ ok: false, errors: [{ path: '', message: 'invoice must be an object', ... }] }`. The README promises that bad input never throws. We already fixed this class of bug for address, name, the vietqr note and numfmt (#110, #111, #142, #95). #143 covered only non-finite totals.

`computeTotals` returns `InvoiceTotals`, not a `Result`, and already reports failures through `totalInWordsError` (see `totals.ts:77-93`). Keep that shape and don't make a breaking change.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `computeTotals(null)`, `computeTotals(undefined)`, `computeTotals('x')`, `computeTotals({})` and `computeTotals({ lines: 'x' })` do not throw.
- [ ] For those inputs the result has `lines: []`, `subtotal`, `discountTotal`, `vatTotal` and `grandTotal` all `0`, `byRate: []`, `totalInWords: ''` and `totalInWordsError` with code `INVALID_INVOICE`, a message (e.g. `Invoice must be an object with a lines array`) and a hint pointing at `validateInvoice`.
- [ ] A line entry that is `null` or not an object does not throw either. Skip it or report it the same way, and document which one in the JSDoc.
- [ ] Valid invoices give exactly the same output as before. Existing tests in `tests/einvoice.test.ts` and `tests/golden/` pass unchanged.
- [ ] New tests in `tests/einvoice.test.ts` cover each input above.
- [ ] Check that `vn-skills einvoice totals` and the `vn_einvoice_totals` MCP tool return the JSON error shape for a file or argument holding `null` and do not crash. Add a CLI or MCP test if either path reaches `computeTotals` unguarded.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.

issues.body:
## Problem
`parseDateInput(input, { lunar: true })` (`packages/core/src/lunar/index.ts:90-122`) allows days 1-30 for lunar input. For day 31 it returns the same message and hint as for a Gregorian date:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json lunar to-solar 31/2/2024
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_DATE","message":"Day 31 is out of range for 02/2024","hint":"Use dd/mm/yyyy or yyyy-mm-dd."}}
```

The input already is dd/mm/yyyy, so the hint doesn't help. The message also reads like a calendar-month check. For a day that only fails the real month length, `convert.ts:229` gives the clearer `Lunar month 2/2025 has only 29 days`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] With `{ lunar: true }`, a day outside 1-30 returns `INVALID_DATE` with a message that names the lunar month, e.g. `Day 31 is out of range for lunar month 02/2024 (lunar months have 29 or 30 days)`.
- [ ] Lunar errors from `parseDateInput` (bad day, bad month, unparseable input) use a lunar-specific hint, e.g. `Lunar dates use dd/mm/yyyy with day 1-30.` Gregorian messages and hints don't change.
- [ ] `lunar to-solar 31/2/2024` with `--json` prints the new message and hint. Add a CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts`.
- [ ] Add a golden case to the lunar fixture in `tests/golden/` if that file supports error cases. Otherwise add a unit test in `tests/lunar.test.ts`.
- [ ] Existing lunar tests pass. `pnpm format` and `pnpm lint` are clean.

issues.title: vietqr: when --amount is shorthand like '50k', say the exact amount to pass instead of a bare INVALID_AMOUNT
issues.body:
## Problem
The README suggests asking for "tạo QR chuyển 500k…", and `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md:70` says `"500k" means 500000`. But the CLI rejects the shorthand without saying what to pass instead:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json vietqr build --bank VCB --account 123 --amount 50k
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_AMOUNT","message":"Amount \"50k\" must be a positive integer in VND","hint":"VND has no decimals; pass e.g. 500000."}}
```

`vn-skills numfmt parse 50k` already reads it as `50000` (`parseAmount` in `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`). The error comes from `buildVietQR` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:92-96`).

A payment amount should not be converted silently, so `buildVietQR` stays strict. The error should say which value to pass.

## Acceptance
- [ ] When `parseAmountString` rejects the amount but `parseAmount` reads it as a positive integer, the `INVALID_AMOUNT` hint names that value, e.g. `"50k" looks like 50000 VND; pass --amount 50000` (for the library: `amount: 50000`).
- [ ] Amounts that `parseAmount` cannot read, or reads as non-integer or ≤ 0, keep today's hint.
- [ ] `buildVietQR` still never builds a QR from shorthand (no silent conversion). Valid amounts behave exactly as before.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/vietqr.test.ts` for `50k`, `1tr2`, `1,5 triệu` (hint names 1500000) and `abc` (old hint).
- [ ] `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md` "Amount is integer VND" says to convert shorthand first (e.g. with `vn-skills numfmt parse`) before passing `--amount`.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
issues.triage_reason: VietQR is the headline skill and "500k" is the README's own example, so newcomers who type it hit this error first. Telling them the exact value fixes it without risking a wrong payment amount.

issues.title: vietqr: return an error instead of throwing when buildVietQR gets null or a non-object
issues.body:
## Problem

`buildVietQR(opts)` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts`, around line 63) reads `opts.bank` at the start without checking that `opts` is an object:

```ts
export function buildVietQR(opts: BuildVietQROptions): Result<BuildVietQRData> {
  const warnings: string[] = [];
  const bank = findBank(String(opts.bank ?? ''));
```

If a caller passes a JSON `null` or no options object at all, the function throws instead of returning the documented `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, hint } }` shape:

```
buildVietQR(null)
→ TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'bank')
    at buildVietQR (packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:63:37)

parseVietQR(null)
→ {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_PAYLOAD","message":"Payload too short to be an EMVCo QR"}}
```

The same kind of call returns `ok:false` from `validateTaxId`, `parsePhone`, `parseCitizenId`, `moneyToWords` and `parseVietQR`. #142 fixed null *notes* only and did not cover the options argument. The README promises: "Every function returns `{ ok: true, ... }` or `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, hint } }` — no exceptions for bad input."

## Acceptance

- [ ] `buildVietQR(null)`, `buildVietQR(undefined)`, `buildVietQR('VCB')`, `buildVietQR(42)` and `buildVietQR([])` return `ok: false` with a stable error code (e.g. `INVALID_OPTIONS`), a message saying an options object is required, and a `hint` that names the required fields (`bank`, `account`).
- [ ] `buildVietQR({})` keeps its current behaviour (`BANK_NOT_FOUND`).
- [ ] Valid calls produce byte-identical payloads, and all existing vietqr tests still pass.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/vietqr.test.ts` cover each input above. If `tests/golden/vietqr.json` and `tests/golden.ts` can express a null or non-object input, also add a golden case there.

When the output is JSON (`--json`, or stdout is not a terminal), `id parse` and `taxid validate` already put warnings in the JSON `warnings` array. They also print each warning as plain text on stderr:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js --json id parse 001099012345 2>&1 >/dev/null | head -3
warning: Format validity does not prove the identity exists.
```

Agents that read stdout and stderr together see every warning twice, and the second copy is not JSON.

The loop sits after the output branch, so it runs in both modes:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/id.ts:35`: `for (const w of r.warnings) process.stderr.write(`warning: ${w}\n`);`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/taxid.ts:26`: same line, same placement.

Other commands do it right. `packages/cli/src/commands/vietqr.ts:51` writes warnings to stderr only inside the human-readable `else` branch.

## Acceptance

- [ ] With JSON output, `id parse` and `taxid validate` write nothing to stderr on success. Warnings appear only in the JSON `warnings` array.
- [ ] With `--pretty` (or a TTY), they still print `warning: …` lines to stderr as today.
- [ ] Check every `process.stderr.write(`warning` in `packages/cli/src/commands/*.ts` and fix any other command that prints in JSON mode (`address.ts:88` and `:148` look correct, but confirm).
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts`: `--json id parse 001099012345` has empty stderr and a non-empty `warnings` array, and `--pretty id parse 001099012345` still writes the warning to stderr. Add the same pair for `taxid validate` with an input that gives a warning.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.

issues.title: vn-holidays: count the working days between two dates (core, CLI `holidays count`, MCP tool)
issues.body:
## Problem

`vn-holidays` answers "is this a working day" (`isWorkingDay`) and "which date is N working days after X" (`addWorkingDays`) in `packages/core/src/holidays/index.ts`. It cannot answer the reverse question: **how many working days are there between two dates?** Typical uses are SLA and deadline checks ("was this processed within 15 working days?"), payroll ("working days in this month") and leave requests. Today an agent has to call `vn_holidays_is_working_day` once per day or guess. Guessing gets Tết, nghỉ bù and swapped Saturdays wrong, and those are the cases this skill exists for.

This needs no new data. It walks the same calendar as `addWorkingDays`, using the existing internal `infoFor(jd)` and the schedules in `packages/core/src/holidays/schedules.ts`.

## Design

Core (`packages/core/src/holidays/index.ts`, exported through `src/index.ts`):

```ts
export interface CountWorkingDaysResult {
  from: string;      // yyyy-mm-dd
  to: string;        // yyyy-mm-dd
  workingDays: number;
  /** false when an unannounced Tết or National Day window was crossed (same meaning as in addWorkingDays). */
  certain: boolean;
}
export function countWorkingDays(
  fromDd: number, fromMm: number, fromYy: number,
  toDd: number, toMm: number, toYy: number,
): Result<CountWorkingDaysResult>;
```

Semantics match `addWorkingDays`: the start date is **not** counted and the end date **is** counted. In other words, it counts working days in `(from, to]`. So if `addWorkingDays(from, n)` returns `to`, then `countWorkingDays(from, to)` is `n`. When `to` is before `from` the result is negative, the mirror of `addWorkingDays` with `n < 0`: it counts working days in `[to, from)` and negates the total. When `from == to` it returns 0.

Errors use the same shapes as the existing functions:
- `INVALID_DATE` for an invalid date, naming which argument is bad.
- `OUT_OF_RANGE` when either date is outside `FIRST_HOLIDAY_YEAR`-`LAST_HOLIDAY_YEAR`, with a message naming the date.
- A new `RANGE_TOO_LARGE` when the two dates are more than 3660 calendar days apart, so a single call stays cheap. The message states the limit.

CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/holidays.ts`): add `holidays count <from> <to>`. Parse the dates the same way as `holidays add`. Output is JSON when piped or with `--json`. Pretty output looks like `12 working days (2026-02-10 → 2026-03-02)`, plus a note when `certain` is false.

MCP (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`): add the tool `vn_holidays_count_working_days` with inputs `from` and `to` (date strings, same format as `vn_holidays_add_working_days`). Its description states the `(from, to]` rule and the meaning of `certain`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `countWorkingDays` is exported from `@vn-skills/core` with the signature and semantics above.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/holidays.test.ts` (at least 10 new cases). Expected values come from the module itself, not hand-typed dates:
  - [ ] Round trip: for several start dates across 2025-2027 (including dates just before Tết and before 2/9) and `n` in {1, 5, 20, 60, -5, -20}, `countWorkingDays(from, addWorkingDays(from, n).date).workingDays === n`.
  - [ ] The count over a range equals the number of days `d` in `(from, to]` where `isWorkingDay(d).working` is true, checked on at least one range that contains a Tết window.
  - [ ] `from == to` gives 0; swapping the arguments negates the result.
  - [ ] `certain` is false for a range that crosses an unannounced year's Tết window, and true for a range inside an announced year.
  - [ ] `INVALID_DATE`, `OUT_OF_RANGE` and `RANGE_TOO_LARGE` are each returned as `ok:false`, with no exception.
  - [ ] Null or non-number arguments return `ok:false` and do not throw.
- [ ] Tests for the CLI command in `tests/cli.test.ts` and the MCP tool in `tests/mcp.test.ts` (one success case and one error case each).
- [ ] `skills/vn-holidays/SKILL.md` documents the command and tool, including the start-excluded/end-included rule. Add the trigger words "đếm ngày làm việc" and "bao nhiêu ngày làm việc" to the description, and add them to `tests/golden/triggers.json` if that file lists vn-holidays keywords.
- [ ] The MCP tool table and count in `README.md` and `README.vi.md` are updated (29 → 30 tools), and `tests/readme.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
issues.triage_reason: This is the natural next question after addWorkingDays (SLA, payroll, leave), and every agent gets it wrong around Tết and nghỉ bù. It reuses existing data with no new facts and makes the holidays skill complete enough to be worth installing. With 0 downloads, one more correct everyday answer gives people a reason to try the skill.

issues.title: vn-holidays: export a year's days off as an iCalendar file (core, CLI `holidays ics`, MCP tool)
issues.body:
## Problem
HR staff, schedulers and agents asked to "thêm lịch nghỉ Tết vào lịch công ty" need the official days off in Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar. vn-skills already has the data: `publicHolidays(year)` in `packages/core/src/holidays/index.ts` returns `daysOff` (holiday / compensatory / swapped), `workingSaturdays`, `pending` and `sources` (URLs in `packages/core/src/holidays/schedules.ts`). There is no way to export them: a grep for `ics` / `VCALENDAR` in `packages/` finds nothing, and the CLI `holidays` command has only `year`, `check`, `add` and `count`.

The best-known competitor, `date-holidays`, has no announced nghỉ bù or swap days for Vietnam (its `VN.yaml` uses a fixed Tết rule). An export that includes those days is something only vn-skills can offer.

The format is defined by RFC 5545: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545.txt. No new Vietnamese facts are needed: export only what `publicHolidays()` returns.

## Proposed surface
- Core (`packages/core/src/holidays/ics.ts`, exported from the holidays index): `holidaysToICS(year: number, options?: { dtstamp?: Date; includeWorkingSaturdays?: boolean }): Result<{ year: number; announced: boolean; ics: string; events: number; warnings: string[] }>`.
  - Pure and offline. Tests pass a fixed `dtstamp` so output is deterministic; default `new Date()`.
  - `BEGIN:VCALENDAR`, `VERSION:2.0`, `PRODID:-//vn-skills//vn-holidays//EN`, `CALSCALE:GREGORIAN`, `X-WR-CALNAME` (e.g. `Ngày nghỉ lễ <year>`).
  - One `VEVENT` per entry in `daysOff`: `UID` stable across runs (e.g. `<date>-<holiday>-<kind>@vn-skills`), `DTSTAMP` (UTC, `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`), `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD`, `DTEND;VALUE=DATE` = next day (exclusive end), `SUMMARY` = Vietnamese `name` (suffix ` (nghỉ bù)` for compensatory, ` (hoán đổi)` for swapped), `DESCRIPTION` with `nameEn` and the year's source URLs when announced, `TRANSP:TRANSPARENT`.
  - With `includeWorkingSaturdays` (default true), one event per `workingSaturdays` date with SUMMARY `Đi làm bù (thứ Bảy)`.
  - Text values escaped per RFC 5545 §3.3.11 (`\\`, `\;`, `\,`, `\n`); lines end in CRLF and are folded at 75 octets per §3.1 without splitting a UTF-8 multi-byte sequence.
  - When `announced` is false, `pending` holidays get no event and each appears in `warnings` (the date is not yet announced).
  - Errors for out-of-range years reuse the existing `publicHolidays` error.
- CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/holidays.ts`): `vn-skills holidays ics <year> [--out <file>] [--no-working-saturdays]`. With `--out`, write the file and print the usual result (JSON when piped: `{ok, year, path, events, announced, warnings}`). Without `--out` and without an explicit `--json`, write the raw ICS text to stdout so `vn-skills holidays ics 2027 > nghi-le-2027.ics` works.
- MCP (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`): `vn_holidays_ics` with `{ year, includeWorkingSaturdays? }`, returning the ICS text plus the summary fields.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `holidaysToICS` exported from `@vn-skills/core`, CLI `holidays ics` and MCP `vn_holidays_ics` exist
- [ ] Tests in `tests/holidays.test.ts` (≥ 10 new cases): the event count equals `daysOff.length` (+ working Saturdays); DTEND is the next day, including across a month end and 31/12; UIDs are stable across two calls; CRLF line endings; no line is longer than 75 octets; a long Vietnamese SUMMARY is folded correctly; an unannounced year gives `warnings` and `announced:false`; an out-of-range year gives the error; escaping of `,` and `;`
- [ ] CLI tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` for `--out` and raw stdout; MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] `skills/vn-holidays/SKILL.md` documents the command and adds trigger words (e.g. "xuất lịch nghỉ", "file ics", "Google Calendar")
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: MCP tool table and tool count updated
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: This is the most concrete thing a calendar user can do with data only vn-skills has: the announced swap and make-up days. It is a visible edge over date-holidays and an easy demo for adoption.
issues.summary: Added holidaysToICS (core, RFC 5545 with escaping, 75-octet UTF-8-safe folding, CRLF), CLI `holidays ics` (--out, --no-working-saturdays, raw stdout), MCP tool vn_holidays_ics, SKILL.md triggers/docs, tool count 31 in READMEs and llms-install.md, and added the new tool to the expected list in tests/mcp.test.ts.

issues.title: vn-money-words: read plain numbers without 'đồng' in the CLI and MCP tool
issues.body:
## Problem
Contracts and invoices also write numbers in words that are not money: "ba mươi (30) ngày", "số lượng: mười hai". Core already has `numberToWords()` (`packages/core/src/money/index.ts:164`), which is `moneyToWords` with `unit: ''` and `chan: false`. Neither the CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/money.ts`, only `money words <amount>`) nor the MCP server (`vn_money_to_words` in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`) exposes it, so CLI and MCP users always get "… đồng". The most-used npm package for this (`read-vietnamese-number`, ~5.6k downloads/month) reads plain numbers by default.

This needs no new domain facts: it reuses the existing reading rules.

## Proposed surface
- CLI: `vn-skills money words <amount> --plain` calls `numberToWords` with the same `--thousand`/`--odd`/capitalize-style options the command already accepts. `--plain` together with any unit or `chẵn` option is a usage error.
- MCP: add an optional `plain: boolean` (default false) to `vn_money_to_words`; when true, call `numberToWords`. Update the tool description to say it also reads plain numbers.
- Negative numbers keep working (`money words --plain -- -5` → `âm năm`, and the existing negative-amount handling in `packages/cli/src/index.ts`).

## Acceptance
- [ ] `vn-skills money words 30 --plain` → `ba mươi`; `105 --plain` → `một trăm lẻ năm`; `0 --plain` → `không`; `--plain --thousand ngàn 1500` uses `ngàn`
- [ ] Golden cases for `numberToWords` added to the money golden fixture in `tests/golden/` (≥ 6 cases incl. 0, 10, 15, 21, 105, 1 000 000) and loaded by the existing golden loader
- [ ] CLI tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` and an MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts` for `plain: true`
- [ ] `skills/vn-money-words/SKILL.md` documents `--plain` with trigger words (e.g. "đọc số", "số bằng chữ", "viết số thành chữ")
- [ ] Default behaviour (with `đồng`) unchanged; existing tests pass
issues.triage_reason: This is a frequent contract-drafting request that core already handles but users cannot reach. It is a small change that closes a gap with the most popular competitor.

issues.title: skill: add vn-text to strip Vietnamese diacritics and make slugs for any text (core, CLI `text`, MCP tool)
issues.body:
## Problem
"Bỏ dấu tiếng Việt" and URL slugs for product names, filenames and article titles are common requests, and LLMs often get `đ/Đ` and stacked tone marks wrong. Core already has `removeDiacritics`, `normalizeText` and `compactKey` (`packages/core/src/shared/diacritics.ts`, exported from `packages/core/src/index.ts`), and they handle `đ/Đ`. But the CLI and MCP server only offer `slugifyName` through `vn-name`, which is for personal names. Nothing exposes general text stripping or slugs. A competing toolkit ships a dedicated package for it (`vn-slugify-plus` in Llein-Dev/viet-dev-toolkit).

No domain facts are needed.

## Proposed surface (new skill `vn-text`)
- Core `packages/core/src/text/index.ts`, exported from `src/index.ts`:
  - `stripDiacritics(text: string): Result<{ text: string }>`: wraps `removeDiacritics`, keeps case, spacing and punctuation.
  - `slugify(text: string, options?: { separator?: string /* default '-' */; maxLength?: number; lowercase?: boolean /* default true */ }): Result<{ slug: string }>`: strip diacritics (đ→d), drop emoji and symbols, collapse runs of non-alphanumerics into one separator, trim separators at the ends, and cut at `maxLength` on a separator boundary without a trailing separator.
  - Non-string / null input → `ok:false` `INVALID_INPUT`; empty or blank → `EMPTY` with a hint (no throws).
  - Do not change `slugifyName` output.
- CLI `packages/cli/src/commands/text.ts`: `vn-skills text strip <text>` and `vn-skills text slug <text> [--separator <s>] [--max-length <n>] [--keep-case]`, registered in `packages/cli/src/index.ts` (update the program description).
- MCP: `vn_text_normalize` with `{ text, mode: 'strip' | 'slug', separator?, maxLength? }`.
- `skills/vn-text/SKILL.md` (name = folder, commands use `npx -y @vn-skills/cli`) with Vietnamese and English trigger words: "bỏ dấu", "không dấu", "chuyển không dấu", "slug", "tạo slug", "remove diacritics", "Vietnamese slug".

## Acceptance
- [ ] ≥ 20 tests in `tests/text.test.ts`: `Đường Nguyễn Huệ` → `duong-nguyen-hue`; uppercase `Đ`; stacked marks (`ỗ`, `ự`, `ặ`); NFD input; emoji and symbols dropped; repeated separators collapsed; `_` separator; `maxLength` boundary; `--keep-case`; empty / blank / null
- [ ] `vn-text` added to the list in `tests/skills.test.ts` and to `tests/golden/triggers.json` (≥ 5 keywords, both languages)
- [ ] CLI tests in `tests/cli.test.ts`; MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: skills table row, MCP tool table and tool count updated
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass; PR title uses scope `skill`

Also added CLI tests (tests/cli.test.ts), an MCP test and tool-list entry (tests/mcp.test.ts), vn-text in tests/skills.test.ts and tests/golden/triggers.json; those were not run. issues.title: vn-lunar: return a month calendar with lunar dates, can chi, solar terms and holidays (core, CLI `lunar month`, MCP…
issues.body:
## Problem
Questions like "tháng này rằm ngày nào?" or "lịch âm tháng 12" need a whole month, but the CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/lunar.ts`: `from-solar`, `to-solar`, `holidays`, `tet`, `canchi`) and the MCP tools convert one date at a time. An agent has to make ~30 calls. The leading competitor `react-native-lich-am` ships a month calendar component. A grep for a month-level function in `packages/core/src/lunar` finds none.

All the parts exist: `lunarInfo` (`lunar/index.ts:53`), `dayCanChi` (`lunar/canchi.ts`), `getSolarTermIndex` (`lunar/astro.ts:302`), `holidays()` (`lunar/holidays.ts:205`) and `publicHolidays()` (`holidays/index.ts:158`). No new domain facts are needed. Giờ hoàng đạo and trực stay out until #205 is resolved.

## Proposed surface
- Core: `lunarMonthCalendar(month: number, year: number): Result<{ month; year; days: Array<{ date: string /* yyyy-mm-dd */; weekday: string; lunar: { day; month; year; leap: boolean }; text: string; dayCanChi: string; firstOfLunarMonth: boolean /* mùng 1 */; fullMoon: boolean /* lunar day 15, rằm */; solarTerm?: string /* only on the day a new term starts */; holidays: string[] /* names from lunar holidays() and publicHolidays().daysOff */ }> }>`. Invalid month/year → `INVALID_DATE`; years outside the supported lunar range return the existing range error. A year outside the vn-holidays range only skips the public days off.
- CLI: `vn-skills lunar month <mm/yyyy>` (also accepts `yyyy-mm`): JSON when piped, a compact table in a terminal.
- MCP: `vn_lunar_month` with `{ month, year }`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] ≥ 12 new tests in `tests/lunar.test.ts`: day count for 28/29/30/31-day months incl. February of a leap year; each day matches `lunarInfo` for the same date; the month containing Tết 2027 (`2027-02-06` per README) flags that day as lunar 1/1 and lists the Tết holiday; a month that spans a leap lunar month (find one with `leapMonthOf`) has `leap: true` on those days; exactly the days where the solar term changes carry `solarTerm`; invalid input `13/2026` and `0/2026`
- [ ] CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts` and MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] `skills/vn-lunar/SKILL.md` documents the command; trigger words "lịch âm tháng", "lịch vạn niên", "rằm tháng này"
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: MCP tool table and tool count updated
issues.triage_reason: The month view is how Vietnamese users read the lunar calendar. Without it the agent needs dozens of calls; with it, the most common lunar question is answered in one call, using only existing functions.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- tests/lunar.test.ts 'flags exactly one rằm per month and mùng 1 at most once or twice': the title is not true of the assertions. It only checks fullMoon >= 1 and that fullMoon equals (lunar.day === 15). It never checks 'exactly one', and it never checks the mùng 1 claim. Make it assert real counts, or rename it and assert firstOfLunarMonth against lunar.day === 1.
- tests/lunar.test.ts 'skips days off for years outside the holiday data': `r.ok || r.error.code === 'OUT_OF_RANGE'` accepts either outcome, so it proves nothing about 2200. The issue requires that a year outside the vn-holidays range only skips public days off. Pick a year that is inside the lunar range but outside the holidays range, and assert ok with no public days off while the lunar holidays are still listed.
- tests/lunar.test.ts 'rejects unsupported lunar years' only checks ok === false. The issue says it must return the existing range error, so assert the specific error code that lunarInfo returns for year 1500.
- The CLI test does not check the invalid-month error code or the 'yyyy-mm' output. The MCP test only checks the day count. Both are thin against the acceptance criteria.
issues.summary: Added lunarMonthCalendar (core), `lunar month` CLI, vn_lunar_month MCP tool, docs (SKILL.md, READMEs, llms-install), and tests; tightened tests per reviewer feedback. Build, typecheck, lint, format and full test suite pass.

issues.title: vn-address: look up wards and provinces by postal code (core, CLI `address postal`, MCP tool)
issues.body:
## Problem
"Mã bưu chính 100000 là ở đâu?" and checking the postal code on shipping forms after the 63→34 merger are common requests. The bundled data already carries `postalCode` on wards and `postalPrefix` on provinces (`packages/core/src/address/data.ts:13,23`, built from thanglequoc/vietnamese-provinces-database via `scripts/build-data.ts`, see `packages/core/data/SOURCES.md`). But these fields are only passed through in convert results (`convert.ts:231`), `provinceInfo` strips `postalPrefix` (`address/index.ts:66`), and no function searches by them.

Use only the bundled fields. Do not add or edit postal data (data changes go through `scripts/build-data.ts`).

## Proposed surface
- Core `findByPostalCode(code: string): Result<{ code: string; wards: Array<{ code; name; postalCode; province: { code; name } }>; provinces: Array<{ code; name; postalPrefix }> }>`.
  - Strip spaces; only digits are accepted.
  - Exact match on ward `postalCode`. Provinces whose `postalPrefix` is a prefix of the input are listed in `provinces`.
  - Empty → `EMPTY`; non-digits → `INVALID_FORMAT`; no match → `NOT_FOUND` with a hint that coverage depends on the upstream dataset. Null / non-string → `ok:false`, no throw.
- CLI: `vn-skills address postal <code>`.
- MCP: `vn_address_postal` with `{ code }`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Before writing tests, count how many wards in `packages/core/data/provinces-2025.json` have a non-empty `postalCode` and state the number in the PR. If it is low, say so in `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` ("postal codes come from the upstream dataset; not every ward has one")
- [ ] ≥ 12 tests in `tests/address.test.ts`, with codes taken from the bundled data (not typed from memory): exact ward match, a code shared by several wards, a province prefix match, spaces in input, empty, letters, unknown code, null
- [ ] ≥ 3 golden cases in the address golden fixture under `tests/golden/`
- [ ] CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts`; MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` documents it with trigger words "mã bưu chính", "mã bưu điện", "postal code", "zip code"
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: MCP tool table and tool count updated
issues.triage_reason: This uses data the package already ships but nobody can query. Postal codes after the merger are a common e-commerce and shipping question that competitors answer.
issues.skip_reason:
gave up after 3 attempts; last: CI gate failed: the coder changed or removed lines of the reproducer test, e.g.:
tests/address.test.ts:       const r = findByPostalCode(v as unknown as string);
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected (the test must be rewritten):
- `findByPostalCode` uses `q.startsWith(p.postalPrefix)`, but the bundled `postalPrefix` can hold several prefixes in one string. Hà Nội has `"10, 11, 12, 13, 14"` in provinces-2025.json. So `findByPostalCode('100000')` never matches the Hà Nội province prefix. Split `postalPrefix` on commas and trim each part before matching, and return that province's prefix in `provinces`.
- The new tests hide this bug. `prefixed` is chosen with `/^\d+$/.test(p.postalPrefix)`, which skips multi-prefix provinces. The golden cases cover only Cao Bằng, whose prefix is `"21"`. Add tests and golden cases for a multi-prefix province, such as a Hà Nội code taken from the bundled data. Also add a province-prefix-only match, meaning a code with no ward match that still lists provinces.
- SKILL.md says all 3,321 bundled wards carry a postal code. I did not verify this, and the issue asks for the actual count of wards with a non-empty `postalCode` to be counted and stated. `data.ts` makes `postalCode` optional and `build-data.ts` sets it to `undefined` when it is missing. Count it from the data, and only keep the claim if it is true.
- The CLI command is declared as `postal <code...>`, but the issue specifies `address postal <code>`. Joining multiple words is arguably fine, but the CLI test does not cover spaced input.

Attempt 2:
CI gate failed: `pnpm lint` failed:
$ eslint .

/home/runner/work/vn-skills/vn-skills/.bot/work/beiryu__vn-skills/241/gate-fix/tests/address.test.ts
  245:34  error  This assertion is unnecessary since it does not change the type of the expression  @typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
  1 error and 0 warnings potentially fixable with the `--fix` option.

[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
issues.summary: Added findByPostalCode (core, handles comma-separated postalPrefix), `address postal` CLI, vn_address_postal MCP tool, SKILL.md/README docs (3321/3321 wards have postalCode, verified), tests and golden cases; fixed the lint error (unnecessary assertion) in tests/address.test.ts. Build, typecheck, lint, format and the full vitest run pass.
issues.repro_notes: Fails because findByPostalCode, the `address postal` CLI command and the vn_address_postal MCP tool do not exist. Tests cover multi-prefix provinces (Hà Nội '10, 11, 12, 13, 14'), a prefix-only match, spaced CLI input and golden cases. All 3321 wards have a postalCode.

issues.title: mcp: give every tool a title and read-only, closed-world annotations
issues.body:
## Problem
The MCP spec (2025-06-18, server/tools: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools) lets a tool declare a `title` and `annotations` (behaviour hints: `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`). Clients and directories use them to show friendly names and to skip or relax confirmation prompts for safe tools. None of the 30 `server.registerTool(...)` calls in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` set them (a grep for `annotations` finds nothing), so clients treat every vn-skills tool as possibly side-effecting and open-world.

Every tool is pure and offline (no file writes or network in `server.ts`; `vietqr_build` returns the PNG inline). So all of them can declare `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`. That is the "offline, no credentials" claim, stated in a form clients can read.

## Proposed change
- Add `title` (short English, e.g. "Build VietQR payload", "Convert address to 34-province format") and the four annotations to every `registerTool` config in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`. Use the field names the installed `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (^1.32.1) types expose. A shared `const OFFLINE_READ_ONLY = {...}` keeps it to one line per tool.
- Tools added later must follow the same pattern; enforce it with the test below.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`: `tools/list` returns every tool with a non-empty `title`, `annotations.readOnlyHint === true`, `destructiveHint === false`, `idempotentHint === true`, `openWorldHint === false`
- [ ] No change to tool names, input schemas or outputs (existing MCP tests pass)
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md MCP section: one sentence that all tools are declared read-only and offline
issues.triage_reason: Directory listings and clients show these hints next to hosted VietQR and e-invoice competitors that need accounts. Declaring every tool read-only and offline backs up vn-skills' main selling point with little effort.
issues.summary: Added a shared OFFLINE_READ_ONLY annotations constant (readOnlyHint true, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint true, openWorldHint false) to all 30 MCP tools (titles already existed); added one sentence to README.md and README.vi.md MCP sections. mcp tests, lint and typecheck pass.

issues.title: mcp: add an opt-in Streamable HTTP mode (`--http`) for shared and remote use
issues.body:
## Problem
`packages/mcp/src/index.ts` only creates a `StdioServerTransport`. Teams that want one shared server, web agent platforms that cannot spawn local processes, and directories that list servers by URL (Smithery's URL publishing path: https://smithery.ai/docs/build/publish) need the standard Streamable HTTP transport (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports). The offline rule is unaffected: the server only listens, makes no outbound calls, and `packages/core` is untouched.

## Proposed change
- `vn-skills-mcp --http [--port 3000] [--host 127.0.0.1]`. Without `--http`, behaviour is exactly as today (stdio).
- Use the SDK's Streamable HTTP server transport (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/streamableHttp.js` in ^1.32.1) in stateless mode (no session IDs; a fresh `createServer()` + transport per request), served with `node:http`. Add no new runtime dependency.
- Endpoint `POST /mcp` (plus the GET/DELETE behaviour the transport defines); other paths → 404.
- Security, following the transports page: bind to `127.0.0.1` by default. Reject requests whose `Origin` header is present and not a localhost origin (403) unless `--allow-origin <origin>` is given (repeatable). Print the listening URL to stderr.
- Dockerfile unchanged. Document `docker run -p 3000:3000 vn-skills-mcp --http --host 0.0.0.0` if the existing ENTRYPOINT forwards args; otherwise adjust the ENTRYPOINT so it does, and update `tests/docker.test.ts` accordingly.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Smoke test in `tests/mcp.test.ts` (or `tests/mcp-http.test.ts`): start `dist/index.js --http --port 0`-style on a free port, send `initialize` then `tools/list` over HTTP, and assert the same tool names as stdio; a foreign `Origin` gets 403; the process is killed after the test
- [ ] Stdio mode tests unchanged and passing
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: a short "HTTP mode" subsection with the command, the localhost default and the Origin note
- [ ] `pnpm lint` passes (no network modules in `packages/core`)
issues.triage_reason: This opens hosted and team use and the URL-based directory path without touching the offline core. It widens where vn-skills can be adopted beyond local stdio clients.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- README.md: the new '### HTTP mode' subsection is inserted before the line 'Other clients: use the generic `mcpServers` block above. AI agents (e.g. Cline) can follow llms-install.md.' That line now sits under the HTTP mode heading, where 'the generic mcpServers block above' no longer reads correctly. README.vi.md places the subsection after that line. Move the HTTP mode subsection in README.md to after the 'Other clients' line so both READMEs match and the Docker section stays intact.
issues.summary: Added opt-in Streamable HTTP mode (--http, --port, --host, --allow-origin) to packages/mcp/src/index.ts, stateless with node:http, localhost Origin check (403), 404 for other paths; stdio unchanged. Documented in README.md and README.vi.md; in README.md the HTTP mode subsection now sits after the 'Other clients' line, matching README.vi.md.
issues.pr_title: feat(mcp): add opt-in Streamable HTTP mode (--http)
issues.pr_body:
Closes #243

## What & why
