proposals.title: vn-holidays: export a year's days off as an iCalendar file (core, CLI `holidays ics`, MCP tool)
proposals.body:
## Problem
HR staff, schedulers and agents asked to "thêm lịch nghỉ Tết vào lịch công ty" need the official days off in Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar. vn-skills already has the data: `publicHolidays(year)` in `packages/core/src/holidays/index.ts` returns `daysOff` (holiday / compensatory / swapped), `workingSaturdays`, `pending` and `sources` (URLs in `packages/core/src/holidays/schedules.ts`). There is no way to export them: a grep for `ics` / `VCALENDAR` in `packages/` finds nothing, and the CLI `holidays` command has only `year`, `check`, `add` and `count`.

The best-known competitor, `date-holidays`, has no announced nghỉ bù or swap days for Vietnam (its `VN.yaml` uses a fixed Tết rule). An export that includes those days is something only vn-skills can offer.

The format is defined by RFC 5545: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545.txt. No new Vietnamese facts are needed: export only what `publicHolidays()` returns.

## Proposed surface
- Core (`packages/core/src/holidays/ics.ts`, exported from the holidays index): `holidaysToICS(year: number, options?: { dtstamp?: Date; includeWorkingSaturdays?: boolean }): Result<{ year: number; announced: boolean; ics: string; events: number; warnings: string[] }>`.
  - Pure and offline. Tests pass a fixed `dtstamp` so output is deterministic; default `new Date()`.
  - `BEGIN:VCALENDAR`, `VERSION:2.0`, `PRODID:-//vn-skills//vn-holidays//EN`, `CALSCALE:GREGORIAN`, `X-WR-CALNAME` (e.g. `Ngày nghỉ lễ <year>`).
  - One `VEVENT` per entry in `daysOff`: `UID` stable across runs (e.g. `<date>-<holiday>-<kind>@vn-skills`), `DTSTAMP` (UTC, `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`), `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD`, `DTEND;VALUE=DATE` = next day (exclusive end), `SUMMARY` = Vietnamese `name` (suffix ` (nghỉ bù)` for compensatory, ` (hoán đổi)` for swapped), `DESCRIPTION` with `nameEn` and the year's source URLs when announced, `TRANSP:TRANSPARENT`.
  - With `includeWorkingSaturdays` (default true), one event per `workingSaturdays` date with SUMMARY `Đi làm bù (thứ Bảy)`.
  - Text values escaped per RFC 5545 §3.3.11 (`\\`, `\;`, `\,`, `\n`); lines end in CRLF and are folded at 75 octets per §3.1 without splitting a UTF-8 multi-byte sequence.
  - When `announced` is false, `pending` holidays get no event and each appears in `warnings` (the date is not yet announced).
  - Errors for out-of-range years reuse the existing `publicHolidays` error.
- CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/holidays.ts`): `vn-skills holidays ics <year> [--out <file>] [--no-working-saturdays]`. With `--out`, write the file and print the usual result (JSON when piped: `{ok, year, path, events, announced, warnings}`). Without `--out` and without an explicit `--json`, write the raw ICS text to stdout so `vn-skills holidays ics 2027 > nghi-le-2027.ics` works.
- MCP (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`): `vn_holidays_ics` with `{ year, includeWorkingSaturdays? }`, returning the ICS text plus the summary fields.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `holidaysToICS` exported from `@vn-skills/core`, CLI `holidays ics` and MCP `vn_holidays_ics` exist
- [ ] Tests in `tests/holidays.test.ts` (≥ 10 new cases): the event count equals `daysOff.length` (+ working Saturdays); DTEND is the next day, including across a month end and 31/12; UIDs are stable across two calls; CRLF line endings; no line is longer than 75 octets; a long Vietnamese SUMMARY is folded correctly; an unannounced year gives `warnings` and `announced:false`; an out-of-range year gives the error; escaping of `,` and `;`
- [ ] CLI tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` for `--out` and raw stdout; MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] `skills/vn-holidays/SKILL.md` documents the command and adds trigger words (e.g. "xuất lịch nghỉ", "file ics", "Google Calendar")
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: MCP tool table and tool count updated
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","priority: p1","size: s"]
proposals.rationale: This is the most concrete thing a calendar user can do with data only vn-skills has: the announced swap and make-up days. It is a visible edge over date-holidays and an easy demo for adoption.

proposals.title: vn-money-words: read plain numbers without 'đồng' in the CLI and MCP tool
proposals.body:
## Problem
Contracts and invoices also write numbers in words that are not money: "ba mươi (30) ngày", "số lượng: mười hai". Core already has `numberToWords()` (`packages/core/src/money/index.ts:164`), which is `moneyToWords` with `unit: ''` and `chan: false`. Neither the CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/money.ts`, only `money words <amount>`) nor the MCP server (`vn_money_to_words` in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`) exposes it, so CLI and MCP users always get "… đồng". The most-used npm package for this (`read-vietnamese-number`, ~5.6k downloads/month) reads plain numbers by default.

This needs no new domain facts: it reuses the existing reading rules.

## Proposed surface
- CLI: `vn-skills money words <amount> --plain` calls `numberToWords` with the same `--thousand`/`--odd`/capitalize-style options the command already accepts. `--plain` together with any unit or `chẵn` option is a usage error.
- MCP: add an optional `plain: boolean` (default false) to `vn_money_to_words`; when true, call `numberToWords`. Update the tool description to say it also reads plain numbers.
- Negative numbers keep working (`money words --plain -- -5` → `âm năm`, and the existing negative-amount handling in `packages/cli/src/index.ts`).

## Acceptance
- [ ] `vn-skills money words 30 --plain` → `ba mươi`; `105 --plain` → `một trăm lẻ năm`; `0 --plain` → `không`; `--plain --thousand ngàn 1500` uses `ngàn`
- [ ] Golden cases for `numberToWords` added to the money golden fixture in `tests/golden/` (≥ 6 cases incl. 0, 10, 15, 21, 105, 1 000 000) and loaded by the existing golden loader
- [ ] CLI tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` and an MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts` for `plain: true`
- [ ] `skills/vn-money-words/SKILL.md` documents `--plain` with trigger words (e.g. "đọc số", "số bằng chữ", "viết số thành chữ")
- [ ] Default behaviour (with `đồng`) unchanged; existing tests pass
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: money","area: cli","area: mcp","priority: p1","size: s"]
proposals.rationale: This is a frequent contract-drafting request that core already handles but users cannot reach. It is a small change that closes a gap with the most popular competitor.

proposals.title: skill: add vn-text to strip Vietnamese diacritics and make slugs for any text (core, CLI `text`, MCP tool)
proposals.body:
## Problem
"Bỏ dấu tiếng Việt" and URL slugs for product names, filenames and article titles are common requests, and LLMs often get `đ/Đ` and stacked tone marks wrong. Core already has `removeDiacritics`, `normalizeText` and `compactKey` (`packages/core/src/shared/diacritics.ts`, exported from `packages/core/src/index.ts`), and they handle `đ/Đ`. But the CLI and MCP server only offer `slugifyName` through `vn-name`, which is for personal names. Nothing exposes general text stripping or slugs. A competing toolkit ships a dedicated package for it (`vn-slugify-plus` in Llein-Dev/viet-dev-toolkit).

No domain facts are needed.

## Proposed surface (new skill `vn-text`)
- Core `packages/core/src/text/index.ts`, exported from `src/index.ts`:
  - `stripDiacritics(text: string): Result<{ text: string }>`: wraps `removeDiacritics`, keeps case, spacing and punctuation.
  - `slugify(text: string, options?: { separator?: string /* default '-' */; maxLength?: number; lowercase?: boolean /* default true */ }): Result<{ slug: string }>`: strip diacritics (đ→d), drop emoji and symbols, collapse runs of non-alphanumerics into one separator, trim separators at the ends, and cut at `maxLength` on a separator boundary without a trailing separator.
  - Non-string / null input → `ok:false` `INVALID_INPUT`; empty or blank → `EMPTY` with a hint (no throws).
  - Do not change `slugifyName` output.
- CLI `packages/cli/src/commands/text.ts`: `vn-skills text strip <text>` and `vn-skills text slug <text> [--separator <s>] [--max-length <n>] [--keep-case]`, registered in `packages/cli/src/index.ts` (update the program description).
- MCP: `vn_text_normalize` with `{ text, mode: 'strip' | 'slug', separator?, maxLength? }`.
- `skills/vn-text/SKILL.md` (name = folder, commands use `npx -y @vn-skills/cli`) with Vietnamese and English trigger words: "bỏ dấu", "không dấu", "chuyển không dấu", "slug", "tạo slug", "remove diacritics", "Vietnamese slug".

## Acceptance
- [ ] ≥ 20 tests in `tests/text.test.ts`: `Đường Nguyễn Huệ` → `duong-nguyen-hue`; uppercase `Đ`; stacked marks (`ỗ`, `ự`, `ặ`); NFD input; emoji and symbols dropped; repeated separators collapsed; `_` separator; `maxLength` boundary; `--keep-case`; empty / blank / null
- [ ] `vn-text` added to the list in `tests/skills.test.ts` and to `tests/golden/triggers.json` (≥ 5 keywords, both languages)
- [ ] CLI tests in `tests/cli.test.ts`; MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: skills table row, MCP tool table and tool count updated
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass; PR title uses scope `skill`
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: skill","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","priority: p1","size: m"]
proposals.rationale: This is one of the most common Vietnamese text tasks given to agents. Core already does the hard part, so a skill with Vietnamese trigger words is cheap and puts vn-skills in front of a much wider audience than payments or addresses.

proposals.title: vn-lunar: return a month calendar with lunar dates, can chi, solar terms and holidays (core, CLI `lunar month`, MCP…
proposals.body:
## Problem
Questions like "tháng này rằm ngày nào?" or "lịch âm tháng 12" need a whole month, but the CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/lunar.ts`: `from-solar`, `to-solar`, `holidays`, `tet`, `canchi`) and the MCP tools convert one date at a time. An agent has to make ~30 calls. The leading competitor `react-native-lich-am` ships a month calendar component. A grep for a month-level function in `packages/core/src/lunar` finds none.

All the parts exist: `lunarInfo` (`lunar/index.ts:53`), `dayCanChi` (`lunar/canchi.ts`), `getSolarTermIndex` (`lunar/astro.ts:302`), `holidays()` (`lunar/holidays.ts:205`) and `publicHolidays()` (`holidays/index.ts:158`). No new domain facts are needed. Giờ hoàng đạo and trực stay out until #205 is resolved.

## Proposed surface
- Core: `lunarMonthCalendar(month: number, year: number): Result<{ month; year; days: Array<{ date: string /* yyyy-mm-dd */; weekday: string; lunar: { day; month; year; leap: boolean }; text: string; dayCanChi: string; firstOfLunarMonth: boolean /* mùng 1 */; fullMoon: boolean /* lunar day 15, rằm */; solarTerm?: string /* only on the day a new term starts */; holidays: string[] /* names from lunar holidays() and publicHolidays().daysOff */ }> }>`. Invalid month/year → `INVALID_DATE`; years outside the supported lunar range return the existing range error. A year outside the vn-holidays range only skips the public days off.
- CLI: `vn-skills lunar month <mm/yyyy>` (also accepts `yyyy-mm`): JSON when piped, a compact table in a terminal.
- MCP: `vn_lunar_month` with `{ month, year }`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] ≥ 12 new tests in `tests/lunar.test.ts`: day count for 28/29/30/31-day months incl. February of a leap year; each day matches `lunarInfo` for the same date; the month containing Tết 2027 (`2027-02-06` per README) flags that day as lunar 1/1 and lists the Tết holiday; a month that spans a leap lunar month (find one with `leapMonthOf`) has `leap: true` on those days; exactly the days where the solar term changes carry `solarTerm`; invalid input `13/2026` and `0/2026`
- [ ] CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts` and MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] `skills/vn-lunar/SKILL.md` documents the command; trigger words "lịch âm tháng", "lịch vạn niên", "rằm tháng này"
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: MCP tool table and tool count updated
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: lunar","area: cli","area: mcp","priority: p2","size: s"]
proposals.rationale: The month view is how Vietnamese users read the lunar calendar. Without it the agent needs dozens of calls; with it, the most common lunar question is answered in one call, using only existing functions.

proposals.title: vn-address: look up wards and provinces by postal code (core, CLI `address postal`, MCP tool)
proposals.body:
## Problem
"Mã bưu chính 100000 là ở đâu?" and checking the postal code on shipping forms after the 63→34 merger are common requests. The bundled data already carries `postalCode` on wards and `postalPrefix` on provinces (`packages/core/src/address/data.ts:13,23`, built from thanglequoc/vietnamese-provinces-database via `scripts/build-data.ts`, see `packages/core/data/SOURCES.md`). But these fields are only passed through in convert results (`convert.ts:231`), `provinceInfo` strips `postalPrefix` (`address/index.ts:66`), and no function searches by them.

Use only the bundled fields. Do not add or edit postal data (data changes go through `scripts/build-data.ts`).

## Proposed surface
- Core `findByPostalCode(code: string): Result<{ code: string; wards: Array<{ code; name; postalCode; province: { code; name } }>; provinces: Array<{ code; name; postalPrefix }> }>`.
  - Strip spaces; only digits are accepted.
  - Exact match on ward `postalCode`. Provinces whose `postalPrefix` is a prefix of the input are listed in `provinces`.
  - Empty → `EMPTY`; non-digits → `INVALID_FORMAT`; no match → `NOT_FOUND` with a hint that coverage depends on the upstream dataset. Null / non-string → `ok:false`, no throw.
- CLI: `vn-skills address postal <code>`.
- MCP: `vn_address_postal` with `{ code }`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Before writing tests, count how many wards in `packages/core/data/provinces-2025.json` have a non-empty `postalCode` and state the number in the PR. If it is low, say so in `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` ("postal codes come from the upstream dataset; not every ward has one")
- [ ] ≥ 12 tests in `tests/address.test.ts`, with codes taken from the bundled data (not typed from memory): exact ward match, a code shared by several wards, a province prefix match, spaces in input, empty, letters, unknown code, null
- [ ] ≥ 3 golden cases in the address golden fixture under `tests/golden/`
- [ ] CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts`; MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`
- [ ] `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` documents it with trigger words "mã bưu chính", "mã bưu điện", "postal code", "zip code"
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: MCP tool table and tool count updated
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: address","area: cli","area: mcp","priority: p2","size: s"]
proposals.rationale: This uses data the package already ships but nobody can query. Postal codes after the merger are a common e-commerce and shipping question that competitors answer.

proposals.title: mcp: give every tool a title and read-only, closed-world annotations
proposals.body:
## Problem
The MCP spec (2025-06-18, server/tools: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools) lets a tool declare a `title` and `annotations` (behaviour hints: `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`). Clients and directories use them to show friendly names and to skip or relax confirmation prompts for safe tools. None of the 30 `server.registerTool(...)` calls in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` set them (a grep for `annotations` finds nothing), so clients treat every vn-skills tool as possibly side-effecting and open-world.

Every tool is pure and offline (no file writes or network in `server.ts`; `vietqr_build` returns the PNG inline). So all of them can declare `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`. That is the "offline, no credentials" claim, stated in a form clients can read.

## Proposed change
- Add `title` (short English, e.g. "Build VietQR payload", "Convert address to 34-province format") and the four annotations to every `registerTool` config in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`. Use the field names the installed `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (^1.32.1) types expose. A shared `const OFFLINE_READ_ONLY = {...}` keeps it to one line per tool.
- Tools added later must follow the same pattern; enforce it with the test below.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`: `tools/list` returns every tool with a non-empty `title`, `annotations.readOnlyHint === true`, `destructiveHint === false`, `idempotentHint === true`, `openWorldHint === false`
- [ ] No change to tool names, input schemas or outputs (existing MCP tests pass)
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md MCP section: one sentence that all tools are declared read-only and offline
proposals.rationale: Directory listings and clients show these hints next to hosted VietQR and e-invoice competitors that need accounts. Declaring every tool read-only and offline backs up vn-skills' main selling point with little effort.

proposals.title: mcp: add an opt-in Streamable HTTP mode (`--http`) for shared and remote use
proposals.body:
## Problem
`packages/mcp/src/index.ts` only creates a `StdioServerTransport`. Teams that want one shared server, web agent platforms that cannot spawn local processes, and directories that list servers by URL (Smithery's URL publishing path: https://smithery.ai/docs/build/publish) need the standard Streamable HTTP transport (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports). The offline rule is unaffected: the server only listens, makes no outbound calls, and `packages/core` is untouched.

## Proposed change
- `vn-skills-mcp --http [--port 3000] [--host 127.0.0.1]`. Without `--http`, behaviour is exactly as today (stdio).
- Use the SDK's Streamable HTTP server transport (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/streamableHttp.js` in ^1.32.1) in stateless mode (no session IDs; a fresh `createServer()` + transport per request), served with `node:http`. Add no new runtime dependency.
- Endpoint `POST /mcp` (plus the GET/DELETE behaviour the transport defines); other paths → 404.
- Security, following the transports page: bind to `127.0.0.1` by default. Reject requests whose `Origin` header is present and not a localhost origin (403) unless `--allow-origin <origin>` is given (repeatable). Print the listening URL to stderr.
- Dockerfile unchanged. Document `docker run -p 3000:3000 vn-skills-mcp --http --host 0.0.0.0` if the existing ENTRYPOINT forwards args; otherwise adjust the ENTRYPOINT so it does, and update `tests/docker.test.ts` accordingly.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Smoke test in `tests/mcp.test.ts` (or `tests/mcp-http.test.ts`): start `dist/index.js --http --port 0`-style on a free port, send `initialize` then `tools/list` over HTTP, and assert the same tool names as stdio; a foreign `Origin` gets 403; the process is killed after the test
- [ ] Stdio mode tests unchanged and passing
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: a short "HTTP mode" subsection with the command, the localhost default and the Origin note
- [ ] `pnpm lint` passes (no network modules in `packages/core`)
proposals.rationale: This opens hosted and team use and the URL-based directory path without touching the offline core. It widens where vn-skills can be adopted beyond local stdio clients.

proposals.title: vn-lunar: list the solar dates of a lunar anniversary (ngày giỗ) for coming years (core, CLI `lunar anniversary`, MCP…
proposals.body:
## Problem

"Giỗ ông là 15/7 âm, những năm tới rơi vào ngày nào?" Death anniversaries, lunar birthdays and other yearly lunar dates are among the most common lunar-calendar questions. Ordinary calendar apps cannot repeat them. Today an agent has to call `lunarToSolar` once per year and handle the edge cases itself. `lunarToSolar(lunarDay, lunarMonth, lunarYear, lunarLeap)` lives in `packages/core/src/lunar/convert.ts` (around line 197), and `lunarMonthLength` and `leapMonthOf` are in the same file. Nothing in core, the CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/lunar.ts`: from-solar, to-solar, holidays, tet, canchi) or `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` returns the next occurrences of a lunar date. Open issues #240 (month view) and #237 (holidays .ics) don't cover this.

Some years have no matching date: the anniversary is on day 30 and the month has only 29 days that year, or it is in a leap month the year doesn't have. The tool must not guess a custom rule for these. Make the behaviour an explicit option that follows the `SKIP` values in RFC 7529 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7529.txt): `OMIT` (the default in RFC 7529), `BACKWARD` and `FORWARD`. Read RFC 7529 for what BACKWARD and FORWARD mean for a missing day and for a missing leap month. Implement exactly that and quote the section in a code comment.

## Proposed surface

- Core, exported from `packages/core/src/lunar/index.ts`:
  `lunarAnniversaries({ day, month, leap? }, { from, count?, skip? }): Result<{ occurrences: Array<{ lunarYear, solar: 'YYYY-MM-DD', lunar: { day, month, leap }, adjusted: 'none' | 'backward' | 'forward' }>, omittedYears: number[] }>`
  - `from` is a solar date `YYYY-MM-DD` (required, so core stays pure and never reads the clock). Return occurrences on or after `from`.
  - `count`: default 5, max 50. `skip`: `'omit' | 'backward' | 'forward'`, default `'omit'`.
  - `leap: false` (default) means the regular month of that number, even in years that also have a leap month with the same number.
  - Return `INVALID_DATE` for day 1-30 / month 1-12 violations, and `OUT_OF_RANGE` when the walk passes the supported year range (1800-2199). Use the same codes and hints as `lunarToSolar`.
- CLI: `vn-skills lunar anniversary <dd/mm> [--leap] [--from YYYY-MM-DD] [--count N] [--skip omit|backward|forward]`. In the CLI only, `--from` defaults to today's date in UTC+7. JSON output when piped, a short table on a TTY.
- MCP: `vn_lunar_anniversary` with the same arguments (`from` required).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Core function, CLI command and MCP tool as above. No new data files and no network.
- [ ] At least 15 tests in `tests/lunar.test.ts` (or a new `tests/lunar-anniversary.test.ts`). Derive expected dates from the existing `lunarToSolar` or existing golden values, never from outside tables. Cover: 1/1 matching the existing Tết golden dates (e.g. Tết 2027 = 2027-02-06); a `from` date after this year's occurrence; day 30 in a 29-day month with each of the three `skip` values; a leap-month anniversary in years with and without that leap month; `count` limits; invalid input; the 2199 boundary.
- [ ] Golden cases added to `tests/golden/lunar.json` (or the lunar golden file in `tests/golden/`) for the pure input → output cases.
- [ ] CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts` and MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`.
- [ ] `skills/vn-lunar/SKILL.md` documents the command and adds trigger words such as "ngày giỗ", "giỗ", "sinh nhật âm lịch". Update `tests/golden/triggers.json` if needed.
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md: MCP tool count and the vn-lunar row of the tools table updated.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.

Out of scope: .ics export (can reuse #237's helper later), giờ hoàng đạo / trực (#205).
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: lunar","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","priority: p1","size: m"]
proposals.rationale: Ngày giỗ and lunar birthdays are an everyday Vietnamese question that calendar apps can't answer. It reuses the existing lunar engine and needs no new facts, because RFC 7529 defines the edge-case options.

proposals.title: mcp: add prompts so the main vn-skills tasks show up as slash commands
proposals.body:
## Problem

Users who install only the MCP server get about 30 tools and none of the workflow guidance in `skills/*/SKILL.md`. They have to know tool names such as `vietqr_build` or `vn_address_convert`. The MCP spec (2025-06-18, server/prompts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/prompts) defines user-controlled prompt templates with `title`, `description` and typed `arguments`. They are served through `prompts/list` / `prompts/get`, and clients such as Claude Desktop and VS Code show them as `/` commands. `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` has only `registerTool` calls: no `registerPrompt` and no `registerResource`. This works with the current `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ^1.x (`McpServer.registerPrompt`) and is separate from #210 (SEP-2640 skills, which needs SDK 2.x).

## Proposed prompts

Add one `server.registerPrompt` per main task (6-8 total), with ASCII names, Vietnamese titles and argument descriptions taken from the matching SKILL.md:

| name | tool it drives | arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tao-vietqr` | `vietqr_build` | bank, account, amount (optional), note (optional) |
| `doi-dia-chi-moi` | `vn_address_convert` | address |
| `kiem-tra-mst` | `vn_tax_id_validate` | taxId |
| `doc-cccd` | `vn_id_parse` | id |
| `so-tien-bang-chu` | `vn_money_to_words` | amount |
| `ngay-lam-viec` | `vn_holidays_add_working_days` | date, days |
| `doi-am-duong` | `vn_lunar_from_solar` | date |
| `kiem-tra-hoa-don` | `vn_einvoice_validate` | invoice (JSON) |

Each `prompts/get` returns one `user` message. It names the tool to call, passes the filled-in arguments, and repeats the key rules from the SKILL.md (e.g. VietQR is offline and not a payment confirmation; tax ID and CCCD validity ≠ registration). Keep the text short. Add no new Vietnamese facts; take wording from the SKILL.md files.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Prompts registered in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` (or a new `packages/mcp/src/prompts.ts` imported there). The server advertises the `prompts` capability.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/mcp.test.ts`: `prompts/list` returns every prompt with a title and description; for each prompt, the tool it names is in `tools/list`; `prompts/get` for `tao-vietqr` with sample arguments returns a message containing those arguments; a missing required argument returns an error.
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md MCP section: a short "Prompts" subsection listing the prompt names.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: MCP-only users currently get no guidance. Slash commands with Vietnamese titles make the server usable without knowing tool names, which helps adoption in Claude Desktop and VS Code. It needs no domain facts.

proposals.title: vn-address: add the economic region (vùng) to provinces and filter provinces by region (core, CLI `address region`,…
proposals.body:
## Problem

"Tỉnh này thuộc vùng nào?" and "Liệt kê các tỉnh Tây Nguyên" come up when splitting shipping zones, sales territories and reports by region. The address data is built by `scripts/build-data.ts` from `thanglequoc/vietnamese-provinces-database`, pinned at v5.2.0 (`8b78ba5`, see `packages/core/data/SOURCES.md`). The build uses `json/simplified_json_generated_data_vn_units_minified.json` and `json/vn_provinces_metadata.json` (build-data.ts lines ~27-32). The upstream README describes an `administrative_regions` table with 8 regions, with Vietnamese and English names, and provinces linked to a region id (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thanglequoc/vietnamese-provinces-database/master/README.md). A search of `packages/core/src/address` and `scripts/build-data.ts` finds no `region`, so this is not imported.

## Source rule (read first)

Take region ids, names and province links **only** from files in the pinned upstream commit. Use the JSON files already used, or another file in the same commit (e.g. the SQL/JSON export holding `administrative_regions`); record any new file in SOURCES.md. Then:
- if the pinned commit has no region data, or
- if any of the 34 provinces lacks a region link,

stop and report what you found on the issue. Do not fill gaps by hand, and do not edit `packages/core/data/*.json` by hand.

## Proposed surface

- `scripts/build-data.ts`: import region `{ id, name, nameEn }` per province into `provinces-2025.json` (or a small `regions` section in it) and re-run `pnpm build-data`; SOURCES.md regenerated with the same pinned SHA.
- Core: `provinceInfo` includes `region`; new `listRegions()`, plus `provincesInRegion(query)`, which matches the region name accent-insensitively via the existing `normalizeText`. Results follow the `Result` shape with `EMPTY` / `NOT_FOUND` errors.
- CLI: `vn-skills address region <province|region>`. A province prints its region; a region prints its provinces.
- MCP: `vn_address_region` with the same behaviour. `vn_address_province` output includes `region`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Region data comes only from the pinned upstream via build-data.ts; SOURCES.md mentions it.
- [ ] All 34 provinces have a region; a test asserts this and that there are exactly as many regions as the upstream lists.
- [ ] At least 20 tests (new `tests/address-region.test.ts` or in `tests/address.test.ts`): lookups with and without diacritics, old province names that map through the existing resolver, every region listed, unknown input, empty input. Expected values come from the built data, not from memory.
- [ ] CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts`, MCP test in `tests/mcp.test.ts`.
- [ ] `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` documents the command, with trigger words such as "vùng", "miền", "Tây Nguyên", "Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long".
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md tool count and vn-address row updated.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: address","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","priority: p2","size: m"]
proposals.rationale: Regions are a common grouping for logistics and reports. The data sits in the dataset vn-skills already pins and cites, so it adds a capability with no new facts. It has an explicit stop if the pinned files lack it.

proposals.title: vn-address: list the old wards that became a new ward (core, CLI `address history`, MCP tool)
proposals.body:
## Problem
"Phường X (mới) gồm những phường cũ nào?" (which old wards make up new ward X?) comes up all the time when HR, CRM and logistics teams match records filed before 01/07/2025 against records filed after it. `convertAddress` answers the forward question (old → new), but nothing answers the reverse one.

The data is already bundled. `packages/core/src/address/data.ts` defines `MAPPING.wards` as `Record<oldWardCode, Array<[newWardCode, boolean]>>`, built old→new by `scripts/build-data.ts` from `tranngocminhhieu/vietnamadminunits` (pinned `7fac8c4` in `packages/core/data/SOURCES.md`). `legacyWardByCode` gives each old ward's district and province, and `wardByCode` gives each new ward's province. No function reads the mapping new→old. The CLI `address` commands are `parse`, `convert`, `convert-file`, `provinces`, `wards` and `province` (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts`), and `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` has no matching tool.

This only inverts data the build already produces. No new facts are needed.

## Proposed surface
- Core (`packages/core/src/address/`, exported from `src/index.ts`): `formerUnits(query: string, options?: { province?: string }): Result<...>`.
  - `query` is a new ward code or a ward name. Resolve names the same way `searchWards` (`packages/core/src/address/index.ts`) does.
  - When `province` is given, search only that province.
  - The result holds the resolved new ward and its province, plus `former`: one entry per old ward that maps to it, with the old ward, district and province (code and full name).
  - Each `former` entry also carries the flag from the mapping tuple, read the same way `convert.ts` reads it. When the old ward was split, the entry lists its other new wards so users can see the split.
  - Build the reverse index lazily, once, from `MAPPING.wards`.
- CLI: `vn-skills address history <ward...> [-p, --province <province>]`. It prints JSON when piped or with `--json`, and a short table otherwise.
- MCP: `vn_address_history` with inputs `ward` and optional `province`. It returns the same JSON as the CLI.

## Errors
- Empty or blank query (or a non-string) → `EMPTY`.
- No ward matches → `NOT_FOUND`, with a hint to add `--province`.
- A name that matches wards in more than one province when no province is given → `AMBIGUOUS`. The hint lists the matching provinces.
- Never throw on null or non-string input.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formerUnits` is exported from `@vn-skills/core` and returns the `Result` shape. It is pure and offline, and no data JSON is edited.
- [ ] A property test: for every old ward code in `MAPPING.wards`, `formerUnits(newCode)` for each of its new codes includes that old ward.
- [ ] At least 20 tests in `tests/address-history.test.ts`, including:
  - a merged ward
  - a ward that took part of a split old ward
  - lookup by code and by name
  - the same name in two provinces, with and without `--province`
  - every error code
  - CLI JSON output
  - the MCP tool
- [ ] Golden cases in `tests/golden/vn-address.json` use the existing file's structure. Expected values are read from the bundled data, not typed from memory.
- [ ] `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` documents the command, with Vietnamese trigger phrases such as "gồm những phường cũ nào" and "trước sáp nhập".
- [ ] The README.md and README.vi.md MCP tool tables and tool count include `vn_address_history`, and `tests/readme.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","area: address","priority: p1","size: m"]
proposals.rationale: Reconciling records from before and after the merger is the main job vn-address users have, and the reverse lookup is the half that is missing. It only inverts bundled data, so it can be built now, and none of the npm address packages offers it, which gives vn-skills a feature they lack.

proposals.title: cli: let `address convert-file --csv` read separate province, district, ward and street columns
proposals.body:
## Problem
Vietnamese CRM and ERP exports usually keep the province, district and ward in separate columns. `vn-skills address convert-file --csv` takes only one free-text column (`--column <name>`, in `packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts` around lines 152-243). Users therefore have to join the columns into one string first, and then the free-text parser has to split them apart again.

Core already accepts structured input: `convertAddress(input: string | ConvertInput)` with `ConvertInput { province: string; district?: string; ward?: string; street?: string }` (`packages/core/src/address/convert.ts`). The MCP tool `vn_address_convert` exposes those fields too. Only the CLI file path lacks them. The upstream dataset offers the same thing (`standardize_admin_unit_columns(df, province, district, ward)`), see https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tranngocminhhieu/vietnamadminunits/main/README.md.

## Proposed surface
Add these options to `address convert-file`, valid only with `--csv`:
- `--province-column <name>` (required whenever any structured column option is used)
- `--district-column <name>`, `--ward-column <name>`, `--street-column <name>` (optional)

Behaviour:
- For each row, call `convertAddress({ province, district, ward, street })` with the named cells. Blank cells are left out.
- The appended output columns stay the same as today: `new_address`, `new_ward_code`, `new_province_code`, `mapping_type`, `confidence` and `warnings`.
- A row with a blank province cell gets the same per-row error form as today (`error: ...` in `warnings`), counts as failed, and leads to exit code 2.

## Errors (JSON when `--json`, like the existing ones)
- `--column` together with any structured column option → `CONFLICTING_OPTIONS`, with a hint to use one or the other.
- A structured column option without `--province-column` → `MISSING_COLUMN`.
- Any structured column option without `--csv` → `MISSING_COLUMN`, with a hint to add `--csv`.
- A named column not in the header → `COLUMN_NOT_FOUND`. The hint lists the available columns, as today.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The new options work as described, and `--column` behaviour is unchanged (existing tests still pass).
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` cover:
  - a CSV with province/district/ward columns, checking that the result equals `convertAddress` on the same structured input
  - province column only
  - province + ward + street columns
  - a blank province cell (per-row failure and exit code 2)
  - each of the error codes above
  - stdin input (`-`)
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md show a structured-columns example next to the existing `convert-file` example.
- [ ] `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` mentions the structured-columns form.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: Bulk migration of stored customer addresses is what the npm address competitors are used for, and most real exports use separate columns. This reuses the structured input core already supports.

proposals.title: vn-money-words: parse Vietnamese number words back to digits (core `wordsToNumber`, CLI `money parse`, MCP tool)
proposals.body:
## Problem
Agents often need to turn an amount written in words, such as "một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng", back into digits. They need it to check contracts and invoices, read scanned documents and compare against a total. `packages/core/src/money/index.ts` only goes one way (`moneyToWords`, `numberToWords`). npm has no Vietnamese words→number parser: searches for "vietnamese words to number" and "vietnamese text to number parse words" return only English or unrelated packages. So this would be a feature only vn-skills offers.

The reading rules already live in `money/index.ts` (`readGroup`, `scaleWord`, the `thousand`/`odd`/`useTu`/`chan`/`unit` options). The parser is their inverse, so it needs no new domain facts.

## Proposed surface
- Core: `wordsToNumber(text: string): Result<{ value: string; negative: boolean; unit: string | null; chan: boolean }>`.
  - `value` is a digit string, so values beyond 2^53 stay exact.
  - Input is NFC-normalised, case-insensitive and tolerant of extra spaces and commas.
  - It must accept every form `moneyToWords` can produce under any combination of its options:
    - `nghìn`/`ngàn`
    - `lẻ`/`linh`
    - `mốt`, `tư`/`bốn`, `lăm`/`năm`
    - `mười`, `mươi`, `trăm`, `không trăm`
    - `triệu`
    - `tỷ`, including repeated `tỷ tỷ` scales
    - a leading `âm`
    - a trailing unit (`đồng` or any other trailing word that is not a number word) and `chẵn`
    - a capitalised first letter
  - Colloquial short forms that `moneyToWords` never produces (for example "trăm rưỡi", or "một trăm năm" meaning 150) are out of scope. Return `INVALID_WORDS` for them instead of guessing.
  - Enforce the same `MAX_MONEY_DIGITS` limit on the result.
- CLI: `vn-skills money parse "<words>"` in `packages/cli/src/commands/money.ts`. It prints `{ ok, value, negative, unit, chan }` as JSON when piped.
- MCP: `vn_money_parse` in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`, input `{ text }`.

## Errors
- Empty or blank text, or non-string input → `EMPTY`.
- An unknown word or impossible order → `INVALID_WORDS`. The message names the first offending word.
- Never throw.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `wordsToNumber` is exported from `@vn-skills/core`.
- [ ] Round-trip property test: `wordsToNumber(moneyToWords(n, opts).words).value === String(n)` for:
  - n = 0..10000
  - a sample of large values, including 10^18 and values with zero groups such as 1000001 and 1000000000001000
  - every combination of `thousand`, `odd`, `useTu`, `chan`, `capitalize` and `unit` ('' and 'đồng')
  - negative values, which give `negative: true`
- [ ] At least 20 named tests in `tests/money.test.ts` or a new `tests/money-parse.test.ts`, covering each error code and the out-of-scope colloquial forms.
- [ ] Round-trip golden cases added to `tests/golden/vn-money-words.json` in a form `tests/golden.ts` loads.
- [ ] `skills/vn-money-words/SKILL.md` documents `money parse`, with trigger phrases such as "đọc số tiền bằng chữ ra số" and "chữ sang số".
- [ ] The README.md and README.vi.md MCP tables and tool count include `vn_money_parse`, and `tests/readme.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","area: money","priority: p1","size: m"]
proposals.rationale: This gives vn-skills a capability no npm package has, and the e-invoice amount-in-words check needs it. It reuses the existing reading rules, so it can be fully tested by round-trip against moneyToWords.

proposals.title: vn-einvoice: warn when a supplied amount in words does not match the grand total
proposals.body:
## Problem
An amount in words ("Số tiền bằng chữ") that disagrees with the digits is a classic invoice mistake, and invoices drafted by an LLM make it too. `computeTotals` (`packages/core/src/einvoice/totals.ts`) writes `totalInWords`, but `validateInvoice` never looks at a value the user supplies: a grep of `packages/core/src/einvoice/schema.ts` for `InWords` finds nothing.

This depends on the issue that adds `wordsToNumber` to `@vn-skills/core` (vn-money-words: parse Vietnamese number words back to digits). Start once that issue is closed.

## Proposed behaviour
- Accept an optional string field `totalInWords` on the invoice input type validated by `validateInvoice`. Inputs without it behave exactly as today.
- When the field is present and the invoice is otherwise valid:
  1. Run `wordsToNumber(totalInWords)`.
  2. If it fails, add a warning with `path: 'totalInWords'`, `severity: 'warning'` and a message naming the unreadable word.
  3. If the parsed value ≠ `computeTotals(invoice).grandTotal`, add a warning with `path: 'totalInWords'` stating both numbers and the expected words from `moneyToWords`.
- Compare numbers, not strings, so the `nghìn`/`ngàn`, `lẻ`/`linh` and `chẵn` variants all pass.
- Use warnings, not errors. Whether a mismatch should block issuing is a legal question this issue does not settle.
- The CLI (`einvoice validate`) and the MCP tool `vn_einvoice_validate` pass the warnings through unchanged.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `validateInvoice` adds the warnings above, and existing einvoice tests still pass.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/einvoice.test.ts` cover:
  - matching words, with no warning
  - matching words that use `ngàn`/`linh`/`chẵn`, with no warning
  - an off-by-one-thousand mismatch, with a warning
  - unreadable words, with a warning
  - a missing field, with no warning
  - the CLI `einvoice validate` JSON output
  - the MCP tool output
- [ ] Golden cases added to `tests/golden/vn-einvoice.json`.
- [ ] `skills/vn-einvoice/SKILL.md` and `skills/vn-einvoice/references/schema.md` document the optional field and the warning.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: This catches a real, common invoice error offline. It is a clear reason to use vn-einvoice instead of letting the model write the words itself.

proposals.title: mcp: expose provinces, wards, banks and holidays as MCP resources
proposals.body:
## Problem
The MCP spec (2025-06-18, server/resources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/resources) lets a server publish read-only data as resources (`resources/list`, `resources/read`) and as URI templates (`resources/templates/list`, RFC 6570). Clients with a resource picker let users attach that data to the chat without the model calling a tool.

`packages/mcp/src/server.ts` has only `registerTool` calls and no `registerResource`. The 34-province list, the wards of a province, the VietQR bank list and a year's days off are reachable only through tools (`vn_address_provinces`, `vn_address_province`, `vietqr_banks`, `vn_holidays_year`). Resources work with the current `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.x (`server.registerResource` and `ResourceTemplate` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js`). No domain facts are needed: each resource returns data core already returns.

## Proposed resources (all `mimeType: application/json`, JSON text bodies)
| URI | Content | Built from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vn-skills://provinces` | the 34 provinces | same function as `vn_address_provinces` (`provincesList()`) |
| `vn-skills://banks` | VietQR bank list | same data as `vietqr_banks` |
| `vn-skills://province/{code}/wards` (template) | the province's info and its wards | `PROVINCES` / `provinceByCode` |
| `vn-skills://holidays/{year}` (template) | the year's days off | same function as `vn_holidays_year` |

- Give each resource a `title` (Vietnamese plus English, for example "Danh sách 34 tỉnh, thành (2025)") and a `description`.
- The `province/{code}/wards` template's `list` callback returns one entry per province.
- An unknown province code, or a year outside the supported range, gives an MCP error that includes the core error's message and hint.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The server declares the `resources` capability, and `resources/list` includes `vn-skills://provinces` and `vn-skills://banks`.
- [ ] `resources/templates/list` includes both templates.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/mcp.test.ts` cover:
  - reading `vn-skills://provinces` gives 34 entries
  - reading `vn-skills://banks` gives the same count as `vietqr_banks`
  - reading `vn-skills://province/<a code taken from PROVINCES>/wards` gives that province's ward count
  - reading `vn-skills://holidays/2026` equals the `vn_holidays_year` result for 2026
  - an unknown code errors
  - an out-of-range year errors
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md get a short "Resources" subsection under "MCP server" listing the URIs, and `tests/readme.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: This uses one more standard MCP feature that directory reviewers and clients surface, and it makes the bundled reference data usable without tool calls. It is small and needs no new facts.

proposals.title: mcp: autocomplete bank and province arguments of the vn-skills prompts
proposals.body:
## Problem
The MCP completion utility (2025-06-18: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/utilities/completion) lets a server suggest values for prompt arguments while the user types. For example, typing "vietc" would suggest Vietcombank and "hà" would suggest Hà Nội. Typos in bank and province names then never reach the tools.

`packages/mcp/src/server.ts` has no completion handler. The data is in core: the bank search and aliases in `packages/core/src/vietqr/banks.ts`, and province search in `packages/core/src/address/index.ts` (`findProvince`, `provincesList`).

**Depends on #250** (MCP prompts). Completion applies only to prompt arguments and resource templates, so start once #250 is closed and the prompts exist in `server.ts`.

## Proposed behaviour
- Wrap each prompt argument that takes a bank in `completable()` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/completable.js`. The callback returns up to 100 suggestions from the existing core bank search, matching code, short name and BIN without diacritics.
- Do the same for each argument that takes a province, matching names without diacritics from the 34-province list.
- Return an empty list for an empty prefix or no match. Never throw.
- The `completions` capability is declared, either by the SDK automatically or explicitly.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Tests in `tests/mcp.test.ts` send `completion/complete` for a bank argument and a province argument:
  - a known prefix includes the expected bank or province, taken from the bundled data in the test
  - an input without diacritics matches
  - an unknown prefix returns an empty list
  - no more than 100 values are returned
- [ ] No new data and no changes to `packages/core/data/*.json`.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: Once prompts land, autocomplete makes them usable without knowing bank codes or exact province names. It reuses existing search functions.

proposals.title: vietqr: find banks by SWIFT/BIC code in findBank, searchBanks, CLI `vietqr banks` and MCP `vietqr_banks`
proposals.body:
## Problem

People ask "<SWIFT code> là ngân hàng nào?" and "SWIFT code của Techcombank". They need this for international transfers and for forms that ask for both the BIN and the SWIFT/BIC. The data is already bundled. `packages/core/data/banks.json` has 43 `swift` values, and the `Bank` type in `packages/core/src/vietqr/banks.ts` declares `swift?: string`. Nothing searches that field, though:

- `findBank()` (`packages/core/src/vietqr/banks.ts`, around lines 97-115) matches the BIN, code, aliases, shortName, keywords and a substring of shortName/name. It never looks at `swift`.
- `searchBanks()` (lines 118-133) filters on bin, code, shortName, name and keywords. It also skips `swift`.
- The text output of the CLI `vietqr banks` command (`packages/cli/src/commands/vietqr.ts`, around line 159) prints bin, code, shortName and name, but not the SWIFT code. JSON output already includes the whole bank object.
- The `vietqr_banks` MCP tool description (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`) only mentions BIN, code, short name and full name.

As a result, a SWIFT query returns nothing, or a wrong substring match.

## What to build

A BIC is 8 characters (4 bank + 2 country + 2 location), or 11 when a 3-character branch code is added. Match case-insensitively on the first 8 characters against the bundled `swift` values. Use only the values already in `banks.json`. Do not add or change any bank data.

Ordering matters. Some aliases and names are also 8 or 11 letters long (for example `vietcombank`, `techcombank`), so they must keep resolving exactly as they do today. Run the SWIFT match **after** the alias, code, shortName and keyword exact matches and **before** the substring fallback.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `findBank(x)` returns the right bank when `x` is a SWIFT code from `banks.json`, in upper or lower case. It also works when `x` is that code followed by a 3-character branch suffix (11 characters total).
- [ ] `findBank('vietcombank')`, `findBank('techcombank')` and every existing alias/code test still return the same bank as before.
- [ ] `searchBanks(swiftCode)` puts the matching bank first.
- [ ] A string that looks like a BIC but matches no bundled `swift` value returns `undefined` from `findBank`, not a substring match on a random bank.
- [ ] CLI `vietqr banks` text output shows the SWIFT code when it exists (an empty column otherwise). `vietqr banks <SWIFT>` finds the bank.
- [ ] The `vietqr_banks` MCP tool description and the `query` describe text mention SWIFT/BIC.
- [ ] `vietqr build --bank <SWIFT>` works because it goes through `findBank`. Add a test for it.
- [ ] At least 8 new test cases in `tests/vietqr.test.ts` (or golden cases in the vietqr golden file). Expected values must come from `packages/core/data/banks.json`.
- [ ] `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md` mentions that banks can be looked up by SWIFT code. Add a Vietnamese trigger phrase such as "mã SWIFT".
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: core","area: vietqr","area: cli","area: mcp","priority: p2","size: s"]
proposals.rationale: The data is already bundled, so this is a cheap new lookup that people need for international transfers. It turns an existing data field into a capability that the VietQR competitors do not advertise.

proposals.title: mcp: export the tool definitions so AI SDK and LangChain apps can use vn-skills tools in-process
proposals.body:
## Problem

Web developers building Vietnamese chatbots or checkouts with the Vercel AI SDK, LangChain.js or the OpenAI SDK cannot use vn-skills tools without running a separate MCP process. The AI SDK docs say stdio MCP should only be used for local servers (https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/mcp-tools). Serverless and Next.js apps therefore have to wrap `@vn-skills/core` functions by hand.

AI SDK tools are plain objects with `description`, `inputSchema` (Zod or JSON Schema) and `execute` (https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/tools-and-tool-calling). `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` already defines all three for each of its 31 tools, but only inline inside `server.registerTool(...)` calls, so nobody else can import them.

## What to build

1. Move every tool definition into one exported table, for example in `packages/mcp/src/tools.ts`. Each entry has `name`, `title`, `description`, `annotations`, `inputSchema` (the Zod raw shape used today) and a handler that returns the **plain JSON result object**, not MCP content.
2. `createServer()` in `server.ts` registers every tool by looping over that table and wraps the handler result with the existing `json()` helper. Behaviour over MCP must stay byte-for-byte the same. The one special case is `vietqr_build` with `image: true`, which also appends the PNG image content. Keep that in the MCP wrapper.
3. Add a subpath export `@vn-skills/mcp/tools` (`exports` in `packages/mcp/package.json` plus a tsup entry). Keep the `bin` entry unchanged. It exports:
   - `TOOLS`, the table
   - `vnTools(options?: { only?: string[] })`, which returns `{ [name]: { description, inputSchema: z.object(shape), execute: async (args) => result } }`. This is the shape the AI SDK `tools` option accepts.
4. Do not add `ai`, `@ai-sdk/*` or `langchain` as dependencies. The returned objects are plain and need only `zod`, which is already a dependency.
5. Importing `@vn-skills/mcp/tools` must not start a server or open stdio.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `import { TOOLS, vnTools } from '@vn-skills/mcp/tools'` works from the built package.
- [ ] A test checks that the names in `TOOLS` equal the names returned by MCP `tools/list` (same set, same descriptions).
- [ ] A test calls `vnTools().vietqr_build.execute({ bank: 'VCB', account: '0011001234567', amount: 500000 })` and gets `ok: true` with a payload starting `000201`.
- [ ] A test calls `vnTools().vn_address_convert.execute(...)` with an old address and gets the same JSON the MCP tool returns as text.
- [ ] A test shows that `vnTools({ only: ['vietqr_build'] })` returns exactly one tool.
- [ ] The existing `tests/mcp.test.ts` and `tests/mcp-http.test.ts` pass unchanged.
- [ ] Add a short "Use in an AI SDK / LangChain app" section with a minimal `generateText({ tools: vnTools() })` example to `packages/mcp/README.md`, `README.md` and `README.vi.md`.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: npm downloads are zero. This makes vn-skills usable inside the web apps of the many JS developers who build on the AI SDK or LangChain and cannot spawn a stdio process, which opens a new way to adopt it. It needs no domain facts.

proposals.title: mcp: ask the user which new ward applies when vn_address_convert finds a split old ward (elicitation)
proposals.body:
## Problem

When an old ward was split across several new wards, `convertAddress` returns `mappingType: 'divided'` and a `candidates` list where exactly one is flagged `isDefault`. Street-level disambiguation is not attempted (see `packages/core/data/SOURCES.md`). The `vn_address_convert` MCP tool (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts`) returns the default plus the candidates. The agent then has to guess or ask the user in free text, and it often silently keeps the default.

The MCP elicitation spec (2025-06-18, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/client/elicitation) lets a server send `elicitation/create` with a flat JSON-schema form (for example a string enum) to a client that declared the `elicitation` capability. The response action is `accept`, `decline` or `cancel`. This request asks only for a ward choice, so it collects no sensitive information. The current SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ^1.32.1) supports this through `server.server.getClientCapabilities()` and `server.server.elicitInput(...)`. A grep of `packages/mcp/src` for `elicit` finds nothing.

## What to build

In the `vn_address_convert` handler only:

- If `r.mappingType === 'divided'` **and** `r.candidates.length > 1` **and** the client declared the `elicitation` capability, call `elicitInput`:
  - The message is in Vietnamese with an English fallback. It names the old ward/district/province and says the ward was split.
  - `requestedSchema` has one required string property `ward` with an `enum` of candidate ward codes and `enumNames` of `"<ward fullName>, <province fullName>"`. Every value must come from `r.candidates`.
- On `accept` with a valid code, set `new.ward` to that candidate, rebuild `new.formatted` the same way core builds it (street, ward, province), mark that candidate `isDefault: true` and the others `false`, and add `chosenBy: 'user'`.
- On `decline`, `cancel`, an invalid code, or an error from `elicitInput`, return today's output unchanged, with `chosenBy: 'default'`.
- If the client does not declare elicitation, or the mapping is not divided, return today's output exactly. Do not add a `chosenBy` field in this case, so existing consumers see no change.
- Leave `vn_address_convert_batch` unchanged (per-row prompting is out of scope).
- Do not change anything in `packages/core`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Tests use an in-memory MCP client (`Client` + `InMemoryTransport` from the SDK) that declares `elicitation` and answers `elicitation/create`:
  - [ ] Accepting a non-default candidate returns that ward in `new.ward`, `new.formatted` contains its name, and `chosenBy` is `'user'`.
  - [ ] Decline and cancel return the default ward and `chosenBy: 'default'`.
  - [ ] The request's enum equals the candidate codes from `convertAddress` for the same input.
- [ ] A test with a client that does **not** declare `elicitation` gets output identical to today's for the same divided address.
- [ ] A test shows that a non-divided address never triggers `elicitation/create`.
- [ ] Use an old ward the bundled mapping marks as divided. Find one through `convertAddress` in the test setup. Do not hard-code ward names from outside the repo.
- [ ] The tool description mentions that the server may ask the user to pick a ward when the client supports it. Update `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` and the README MCP section (EN + VI) in one sentence each.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: When an old ward was split, the tool can only return a default today, which may be wrong. Asking the user fixes that in clients that support elicitation and changes nothing elsewhere. It uses only the pinned mapping, so no new facts are needed.

proposals.title: mcp: show an inline VietQR card for vietqr_build in MCP Apps clients
proposals.body:
## Problem

`vietqr_build` in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` returns JSON text plus a PNG image. In Claude, ChatGPT and VS Code the user sees a block of JSON and a bare image, with no bank, account or amount next to it and no way to copy the account number.

MCP Apps is the official MCP extension for interactive UI (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps, spec version 2026-01-26, npm `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`). A tool points to a `ui://` HTML resource. The host renders that resource in a sandboxed iframe and passes the tool result to it. The ext-apps README lists ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose, Postman and MCPJam as supported hosts. Hosts without Apps support ignore the link and show today's output unchanged.

No file in `packages/` mentions `ui://` or an app resource today.

## What to build

One view to start with: a VietQR card.

- Add a self-contained HTML view, for example `packages/mcp/src/apps/vietqr.html`, and include it in the build output. It shows the QR image from the tool result, the bank short name and BIN, the account, the amount formatted as VND (`1.200.000 ₫`, the same format as `formatVnd` in core) and the note. Add a copy button for the account number and one for the payload.
- Register the view as a resource `ui://vn-skills/vietqr`. Use the mime type and resource metadata that the MCP Apps spec requires. Read the spec linked from the ext-apps README; do not guess the field names.
- Link `vietqr_build` to the view through the tool `_meta` field that the spec defines (the UI resource URI).
- The view gets the tool result through the host bridge that the spec describes. Use the app-side API of `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` if it works with the current `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ^1.x server. If it does not, implement the documented postMessage protocol directly. Do not migrate the server to SDK 2.x in this issue; that decision belongs to #210.
- Offline rule: the HTML must not load scripts, styles, fonts or images from any network origin. Inline everything. The QR image comes from the PNG that `vietqr_build` already returns, so the view does not need a QR library.
- Leave `packages/core` untouched. The text and image content of `vietqr_build` must stay exactly as it is today.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `resources/list` on the MCP server includes `ui://vn-skills/vietqr` with the mime type the MCP Apps spec requires
- [ ] `resources/read` for that URI returns the HTML, and a test checks that the HTML has no `http://` or `https://` script, style, font or image references
- [ ] `tools/list` shows `vietqr_build` carrying the spec's UI resource link in `_meta`; every other tool is unchanged
- [ ] Existing `tests/mcp.test.ts` assertions on the `vietqr_build` output still pass unchanged
- [ ] New tests in `tests/mcp.test.ts` (or a new `tests/mcp-apps.test.ts`) cover the three points above
- [ ] The view renders the card when opened with a sample tool result. Describe in the PR how you checked this, for example with the ext-apps basic host example or MCPJam
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md say in one or two lines that MCP Apps hosts show a VietQR card
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: A scannable QR card inside Claude or ChatGPT is the clearest demo of what vn-skills does, and it shows up in every screenshot and directory listing. It needs no Vietnamese domain facts, does not depend on the SDK 2.x decision, and hosts without Apps support see no change.

proposals.title: vietqr: let callers add or override banks at runtime (core registerBanks, CLI --banks, MCP --banks)
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","area: vietqr","priority: p2","size: m"]
proposals.rationale: VietQR is the most-used part of the toolkit, and today users with renamed banks or wallets get 'no bank match' with no workaround while #203 waits on a source. Letting callers bring their own entries unblocks them without vn-skills stating any new bank facts.

proposals.title: vn-einvoice: split a VAT-inclusive price into net and VAT (core, CLI `einvoice vat`, MCP tool)
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","area: einvoice","priority: p2","size: s"]

proposals.title: sheets: build a Google Sheets custom-functions bundle from @vn-skills/core (VN_TIEN_CHU, VN_MST, VN_DIA_CHI_MOI, …)
proposals.body:
## Problem
The people who convert addresses, write amounts in words and check tax IDs are often accountants and office staff working in spreadsheets, without Node, MCP or an agent. Google Apps Script supports custom functions: plain JavaScript marked `@customfunction`, called like built-in formulas. Google recommends processing whole ranges as arrays (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/sheets/functions).

`@vn-skills/core` is pure TypeScript with bundled data and no network access, so it can be bundled into one script. The repo has no Sheets or Apps Script target.

## Proposed surface
- A new private workspace package, `packages/sheets` (`"private": true`; it is not published to npm), with:
  - `src/functions.ts`: wrappers with JSDoc `@customfunction` and Vietnamese descriptions:
    - `VN_TIEN_CHU(amount, [thousand])` → `moneyToWords`
    - `VN_SO_THANH_CHU(number)` → `numberToWords`
    - `VN_MST(taxId)` → TRUE/FALSE from `validateTaxId`
    - `VN_AM_LICH(date)` → lunar text from `lunarInfo`
    - `VN_NGAY_LAM_VIEC(date)` → TRUE/FALSE
    - `VN_CONG_NGAY_LAM_VIEC(date, n)` → a date from `addWorkingDays`
    - `VN_DIA_CHI_MOI(address)` → `convertAddress(...).new.formatted`
  - Every wrapper accepts a single value or a 2-D range and returns the same shape. On `ok:false` a wrapper returns the error message text instead of throwing, so one bad cell does not break the column.
  - Dates: accept a JS `Date` (what Sheets passes) or a `dd/mm/yyyy` string. Read the day, month and year from the Date with the script time zone. Ship an `appsscript.json` with `"timeZone": "Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh"`.
  - A build script that writes one IIFE bundle per variant to `packages/sheets/dist/`: `vn-skills.gs` (all functions) and `vn-skills-lite.gs` (without the address functions and data). Use the bundler the repo already uses if it fits; otherwise add `esbuild` as a devDependency of this package only.
- Do not change release config in this issue. Attaching the files to GitHub Releases is a later maintainer step.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `pnpm --filter ./packages/sheets build` produces both `.gs` files plus `appsscript.json`. The build is wired into the root `pnpm build` only if that does not slow CI noticeably; otherwise it runs in its test.
- [ ] `tests/sheets.test.ts` loads each built bundle in a Node `vm` context with no `require` and no network, and calls the global functions. It covers:
  - a single value and a 2-D range for each function;
  - an error cell returned as text;
  - a Date input and a string date;
  - the lite bundle not defining `VN_DIA_CHI_MOI`.
- [ ] The README says how to install the bundle: Extensions → Apps Script, paste the file, set the time zone. Write it in `README.md` and `README.vi.md`, with a formula example per function. It reports both bundle sizes as measured by the build. It does not claim Apps Script limits that are not in Google's docs. If the full bundle seems too large, recommend the lite bundle.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: Today vn-skills only reaches people who run Node or an agent. Spreadsheet formulas reach the accountants who actually do bulk address conversion and amount-in-words work, a new adoption channel with no competitor in this niche.

proposals.title: vn-address: return the converted address in English from the bundled nameEn data (core, CLI --en, MCP)
proposals.body:
## Problem
Exporters, visa and travel forms, international shipping labels and English-language apps need a converted address in English, and an agent asked to "translate this address" after a 63→34 conversion has nothing to call. The English names are already bundled: `scripts/build-data.ts:233` and `:244` import `NameEn` for wards and provinces from the pinned `thanglequoc/vietnamese-provinces-database` v5.2.0 (see `packages/core/data/SOURCES.md`), and `Ward.nameEn` / `Province.nameEn` are declared in `packages/core/src/address/data.ts:9,19`. Examples in the data: Hà Nội → `Hanoi`, Phường Ba Đình → `Ba Dinh`.

Nothing outputs them. `formatAddress` (`packages/core/src/address/index.ts:104`) and the `formatted` strings in `packages/core/src/address/convert.ts` (lines 116, 139, 181, 202) and `parse.ts:216` only join the Vietnamese `fullName`. `nameEn` reaches users only through `provinceInfo`.

## Scope
- Only use the `nameEn` values already in `packages/core/data/provinces-2025.json`. Do **not** add English unit words ("Ward", "Commune", "City", …) unless the pinned upstream release already provides full English names. In that case, import them through `scripts/build-data.ts` and record the change in `SOURCES.md`, without editing the JSON by hand. Otherwise output the bare names (`12 Nguyen Hue, Sai Gon, Ho Chi Minh City` style, using whatever `nameEn` holds).
- If a ward or province has no `nameEn`, fall back to `removeDiacritics(name)` (`packages/core/src/shared/diacritics.ts`) and add a warning that names the unit.
- Keep the street as the user typed it, with diacritics removed.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formatAddress(parts, { lang: 'en' })` returns the English form. The default stays `'vi'` with unchanged output.
- [ ] `convertAddress` results gain `new.formattedEn` (additive; `new.formatted` is unchanged). `parseAddress2025` results gain `formattedEn` too.
- [ ] `conversionFields` (convert.ts:216) includes `formattedEn`, so `vn_address_convert` and `vn_address_convert_batch` return it with no new input.
- [ ] CLI: `vn-skills address convert --en …` prints the English line in pretty mode (JSON always has the field). `address convert-file --csv --en` appends a `new_address_en` column. Without `--en`, the CSV columns are unchanged.
- [ ] `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` mentions the English output, with trigger words such as "địa chỉ tiếng Anh" and "English address".
- [ ] ≥ 20 tests in `tests/address-en.test.ts` (Hà Nội, TP.HCM, a commune, a special zone if present, missing-nameEn fallback, street with diacritics, CLI `--en`, CSV column, MCP field), plus golden cases in `tests/golden/` for the pure input → output cases.
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md mention `--en` in the vn-address row or bulk-convert section.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","area: address","priority: p1","size: m"]
proposals.rationale: English output uses data that is already bundled but never shown. It answers a frequent request after the 63→34 conversion that the address competitors do not cover.

proposals.title: vn-address: check that a ward belongs to a province (core validateAddress, CLI `address validate`, MCP tool)
proposals.body:
## Problem Checkout and onboarding forms with province and ward dropdowns, and imported records that carry codes, need to confirm the ward really is in the given province after the 01/07/2025 reform. The public address API (`packages/core/src/address/index.ts`: `findProvince`, `provinceInfo`, `provincesList`, `lookupProvince`, `searchWards`, `formatAddress`, `formerUnits`) has no hierarchy check by code or name. The MCP address tools convert or search, but none validates a structured `{province, ward}` pair. Competitor `vietnam-address-kit` (about 1.1k downloads a month) offers `validateHierarchy({ provinceCode, wardCode })`. ## Proposed surface `validateAddress({ province, ward })` in `packages/core/src/address/validate.ts`, exported from `src/address/index.ts`. Both fields accept a code or a name, matched the same way as `findProvince` and `searchWards`. Return shape (Result): - `ok: false` with `EMPTY` when either field is blank or not a string. It must not throw on null or non-object input. - `ok: true, valid: true, province, ward` (summaries with code/name/fullName) when the ward is in the province. - `ok: true, valid: false, reason`, with `reason` one of: - `PROVINCE_NOT_FOUND` - `WARD_NOT_FOUND`: no current or legacy ward matches. - `WARD_NOT_IN_PROVINCE`: the ward exists in another current province. Include `suggestions`: up to 5 `{ward, province}` from `searchWards(ward)` with an exact match. - `LEGACY_WARD`: the name is a pre-2025 ward of that (old or current) province. Include the new ward(s) from `convertAddress({ province, ward })`, flagging divided wards. Use only bundled data (`provinces-2025.json`, `legacy-63.json`, `mapping-old-new.json`). ## Acceptance - [ ] Core function and types exported from `@vn-skills/core`. - [ ] CLI `vn-skills address validate --province

--ward ` with JSON and pretty output. Exit code 0 when valid, 2 when `valid: false`. - [ ] MCP tool `vn_address_validate` in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` with title and read-only, closed-world annotations like the other tools.
