proposals.title: cli: add --out and a --report migration summary to `address convert-file`
proposals.body:
## Problem
When migrating a customer table, users need an audit trail: how many rows converted, how many were divided or low-confidence, and which rows need review. `address convert-file` (`packages/cli/src/commands/address.ts:164-305`) writes rows to stdout. It prints only `converted N, failed M` on stderr when something fails. It has no output-file option and no report, so users compute totals and pick review rows themselves. The MCP batch tool already returns a `summary` `{ total, converted, failed }` (`convertAddresses` in `packages/core/src/address/convert.ts:262`), so the CLI is the odd one out. Competitor `vietnam-address-kit` ships `migrate … --out … --report report.json`.

## Proposed surface
- `--out <file>`: write the CSV/NDJSON to this file instead of stdout.
- `--report <file.json>`: write a JSON report:
  - `{ total, converted, failed }`
  - `byMappingType`: count per `mappingType` value
  - `confidence` buckets `<0.5`, `0.5–0.7`, `0.7–0.9`, `≥0.9`
  - `withWarnings`
  - `review`: rows with `ok:false` or `confidence < --review-below`

  Each `review` entry is `{ row, input, reason }`. `row` is the line number in text mode and the 1-based data row (header excluded) in CSV mode.
- `--review-below <n>`: confidence threshold, default `0.7`, must be in [0,1]. Otherwise exit with `INVALID_OPTION` JSON in `--json` mode.
- `--only-review`: emit only the rows that land in `review`.

Existing behaviour without these flags (output, exit code 2 on failures, stderr line) stays the same. Write errors on `--out`/`--report` return `WRITE_ERROR` in the same `{ok:false,error:{code,message,hint}}` shape as `READ_ERROR`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Flags work in both text (NDJSON) and `--csv` modes, including the structured `--province-column` mode.
- [ ] Report counts add up (`converted + failed === total`, buckets sum to `converted`).
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` (or a new `tests/convert-file-report.test.ts`) use a temp dir and cover: `--out`, `--report` contents, `--review-below` validation, `--only-review`, `WRITE_ERROR`, and unchanged output without flags.
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md bulk-convert snippets show `--out … --report report.json`. `skills/vn-address/SKILL.md` mentions the report.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: Bulk migration of old addresses is the main job for vn-address. A report makes the CLI usable for real data migrations and matches what the leading competitor offers.

proposals.title: vn-lunar: turn Vietnamese date phrases into dates, including lunar ones like 'rằm tháng Giêng' (core, CLI `lunar…
proposals.body:
## Problem
Users ask with phrases, not numbers: "rằm tháng 7", "mùng 1 Tết năm sau", "ngày 23 tháng Chạp", "thứ Sáu tuần sau", "3 ngày nữa". `parseDateInput` (`packages/core/src/lunar/index.ts:150`) accepts only numeric `dd/mm/yyyy` and `yyyy-mm-dd`, and no CLI command or MCP tool takes a phrase. All the parts exist already: lunar ↔ solar conversion (`lunarToSolar`, `solarToLunar`), the lunar month names Giêng … Chạp (`packages/core/src/lunar/canchi.ts:100`) and the named lunar festivals (`packages/core/src/lunar/holidays.ts`). chrono-node has a Vietnamese locale for Gregorian relative phrases, but nothing handles lunar phrases. This is pure language convention, with no legal facts.

## Proposed surface
`parseVietnameseDate(text, { ref?: 'yyyy-mm-dd' })` in `packages/core/src/lunar/phrase.ts`, exported from core. `ref` defaults to today in UTC+7. It returns a Result:

```
{ ok: true, solar: 'yyyy-mm-dd', lunar?: {day, month, year, leap}, calendar: 'solar'|'lunar', matchedText, rule }
```

It returns `EMPTY` or `UNRECOGNISED` errors with a hint listing the supported forms. It must not throw on null input.

Supported forms, with and without diacritics and case-insensitive. Document this list in SKILL.md:
- Lunar dates:
  - `ngày D tháng M âm`, `D/M âm`, `D/M âm lịch`
  - `mùng D tháng M`, `rằm tháng M` (= day 15)
  - `tháng Giêng` (= 1), `tháng Chạp` (= 12), `tháng Một` (= 11) as month words
  - an optional `nhuận` after the month
- Lunar festivals: the names already in `lunar/holidays.ts` (e.g. "Tết", "mùng 1 Tết", "Rằm tháng Giêng", "Tết Trung thu", "Vu Lan"), matched by the existing names only.
- Year qualifiers: `năm nay`, `năm sau`, `năm ngoái`, `năm YYYY`. These refer to the lunar year for lunar phrases and to the solar year otherwise.
- Relative forms:
  - `hôm nay`, `ngày mai`, `ngày kia`, `hôm qua`
  - `N ngày nữa`, `N ngày trước`, `N tuần nữa`
  - `thứ Hai … Chủ nhật` with `này`, `tuần này`, `tuần sau`, `tuần trước`. Weeks run Monday–Sunday; state this in the docs.
- Gregorian: `ngày D tháng M năm Y`, plus whatever `parseDateInput` already accepts.

Document these conventions in SKILL.md:
- A lunar phrase without a year means the next occurrence on or after `ref`.
- A leap month that does not exist in the target year returns `INVALID_DATE` with a hint. Do not guess.
- Day 30 in a 29-day lunar month also returns `INVALID_DATE` with a hint.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Core function exported and covered by ≥ 20 tests in `tests/lunar-phrase.test.ts`, with a fixed `ref`: every form above; a phrase without diacritics; a leap month that exists (e.g. a year with a leap month already in the lunar tests) and one that doesn't; a next-occurrence rollover; empty/null input.
- [ ] Golden cases in `tests/golden/` for pure phrase+ref → date.
- [ ] CLI `vn-skills lunar parse "rằm tháng Giêng năm sau" [--ref 2026-10-28]`.
- [ ] MCP tool `vn_lunar_parse_date` (`text`, optional `ref`) with title and read-only annotations. README tool table and count updated (EN + VI).
- [ ] `skills/vn-lunar/SKILL.md` lists the supported phrases and trigger words ("rằm tháng", "mùng 1", "ngày âm").
- [ ] No new runtime dependency (no chrono-node). `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.labels: ["type: feature","area: core","area: cli","area: mcp","area: lunar","priority: p2","size: m"]
proposals.rationale: Lunar phrases are how Vietnamese users ask about dates, and no JS library parses them. The parser connects plain speech to the existing lunar, holiday and working-day tools.

proposals.title: n8n: add a 'Vietnam Toolkit' community node package built on @vn-skills/core
proposals.body:
## Problem
Vietnamese ops and accounting teams who automate in n8n have no node for VietQR, the 63→34 address conversion, tax IDs or amounts in words. An npm search for n8n community nodes with 'vietnam' (2026-10-28) found only unrelated packages. `n8n-nodes-base` gets about 368k downloads a month. The checkout has no n8n target. vn-skills core is offline and needs no credentials, so it is a good fit for an n8n node.

## n8n requirements (from https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/creating-nodes/deploy/submit-community-nodes/)
- Package name starts with `n8n-nodes-` or `@<scope>/n8n-nodes-`: use `@vn-skills/n8n-nodes-vn-skills`.
- `keywords` include `n8n-community-node-package`.
- Nodes are declared under the `n8n` key in package.json (`n8nNodesApiVersion`, `nodes: ["dist/nodes/VnSkills/VnSkills.node.js"]`).
- `n8n-workflow` is a peer dependency, not bundled.

## Proposed surface
New workspace package `packages/n8n` with one node, `Vietnam Toolkit` (`VnSkills.node.ts`), with no credentials. Each resource/operation calls `@vn-skills/core` directly:
- VietQR: Build (bank, account, amount, note → payload), Parse (payload)
- Address: Convert (text)
- Tax ID: Validate
- Citizen ID: Parse
- Money: To Words (amount)
- Holidays: Is Working Day (date), Add Working Days (date, n)

Put the operation logic in a pure `operations.ts` (input object → core Result) so it can be tested without n8n. `execute()` maps items through it. Core `ok:false` results are returned as item JSON, or thrown as `NodeOperationError` when "Continue On Fail" is off.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `packages/n8n` builds with the workspace `pnpm build`. Its package.json has the name, keyword and `n8n` fields above, plus `license: MIT` and a `repository` field.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/n8n.test.ts`:
  - one per operation through `operations.ts`
  - the node `description.properties` lists every operation
  - the `n8n.nodes` path exists after build
  - an error case per resource
- [ ] `packages/n8n/README.md` shows install ("Settings → Community Nodes → @vn-skills/n8n-nodes-vn-skills") and one workflow example. Add a short n8n section to README.md and README.vi.md.
- [ ] Do not change `.github/workflows/` or release config. Leave a note in the PR that adding the package to release-please and npm publishing (with provenance, required for n8n verification) is a follow-up for the maintainer.
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass.
proposals.rationale: No n8n node covers this yet. An n8n node reaches automation users who never install an agent or MCP client, which is a new way for people to find and adopt the project.

proposals.title: repo: add a static browser playground built on @vn-skills/core (VietQR, address, tax ID, CCCD, money words, lunar)
proposals.body:
## Problem
Someone comparing Vietnam libraries cannot try vn-skills without installing Node, the CLI or an MCP client. Both address competitors ship a browser playground: vietnam-address-kit links one at zindont.github.io/vietnam-address-kit, and Llein-Dev/viet-dev-toolkit has a 5-tab live playground. The repo has none, and a grep for `playground` and `github.io` finds nothing. RM-025 (docs site) is still `idea`.

`@vn-skills/core` is pure, offline TypeScript with bundled data, so a static page can import it directly with no backend. The page also shows that the toolkit really is offline.

## Scope
Add a new private workspace package `packages/playground` (not published to npm):

- Build it with Vite as a static site. `pnpm --filter ./packages/playground build` writes `packages/playground/dist/` (index.html plus assets). `pnpm --filter ./packages/playground dev` runs it locally.
- Use one tab per main skill, each with a form and the JSON `Result` shown below it:
  - **VietQR**: `buildVietQR` (bank, account, amount, note) and `parseVietQR` (paste a payload). Show the payload. Show a QR image only if core already exports a renderer; otherwise show the payload text.
  - **Địa chỉ**: `convertAddress` (old → new, 34 provinces). Load the address data lazily with a dynamic `import()` so the first page load stays small.
  - **MST**: `validateTaxId`.
  - **CCCD**: `parseCitizenId`, with a visible note that format validity does not prove the identity exists and that IDs never leave the browser.
  - **Tiền bằng chữ**: `moneyToWords`.
  - **Âm lịch**: `lunarInfo` for a picked solar date.
- Put the logic in plain functions in `packages/playground/src/handlers.ts` (form input → core call → result). Keep the UI thin and avoid a framework if possible, so the handlers can be tested in Node.
- Make no network requests at runtime: no CDN scripts, fonts or analytics. Bundle every asset.
- Use Vietnamese UI labels with English in parentheses.
- Set Vite `base` to `./` so the build works under any GitHub Pages path.

## Out of scope
Deploying to GitHub Pages changes `.github/workflows/`, so the maintainer will do it in a separate change. Do not edit workflows here.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `packages/playground` exists, is `private: true`, and builds with `pnpm --filter ./packages/playground build`
- [ ] Six tabs work (VietQR build/parse, address convert, tax ID, CCCD, money in words, lunar), each calling `@vn-skills/core`
- [ ] Address data is loaded through a dynamic import, not in the entry chunk
- [ ] `tests/playground.test.ts` has at least 10 cases that call `handlers.ts` for every tab, plus a smoke test that runs the build and checks that `dist/index.html` exists and that the built JS has no `http://` or `https://` script, font or fetch URLs
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md get a short "Try it in the browser" section with the local `dev` command
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: With 0 stars, newcomers need a zero-install way to try vn-skills, and both direct competitors already offer one. Everything it needs is already in core.

proposals.title: sheets: add an Excel custom-functions add-in (packages/excel) reusing the Sheets wrappers
proposals.body:
## Problem
`packages/sheets` (#272, PR #274) gives Google Sheets users formulas such as `=VN_TIEN_CHU(A2)` and `=VN_MST(A2:A9)`. Most Vietnamese accountants and office staff work in Excel, which has no equivalent. A grep finds no Excel or Office add-in target.

Microsoft's docs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/dev/add-ins/excel/custom-functions-overview) describe Excel custom functions as JavaScript/TypeScript functions marked `@customfunction`, shipped as an Office Add-in (manifest + functions JS + functions.json metadata + an HTML page). This is the same model as Apps Script, so the wrappers in `packages/sheets/src/functions.ts` can be reused.

## Scope
Add a new private package `packages/excel`:

- **Wrappers.** Reuse the wrapper logic from `packages/sheets/src/functions.ts` and `packages/sheets/src/shared.ts` by importing it or moving shared parts to a common file; do not copy the logic.
- **Function names.** Expose the functions under the namespace `VN`:
  - `VN.TIEN_CHU(amount, [thousand])`
  - `VN.SO_THANH_CHU(number)`
  - `VN.MST(taxId)`
  - `VN.AM_LICH(date)`
  - `VN.NGAY_LAM_VIEC(date)`
  - `VN.CONG_NGAY_LAM_VIEC(date, n)`
- **Ranges.** Every function accepts a single value or a range (Excel passes ranges as 2-D arrays) and returns the same shape. A bad cell returns the error text, as in Sheets.
- **Dates.** Excel passes dates as serial numbers (days since 1899-12-30), not Date objects. Convert numeric date arguments from serial days; `dd/mm/yyyy` text keeps working.
- **Address function.** Measure the bundle size first. Add `VN.DIA_CHI_MOI(address)` only if the bundle with address data builds and the size is reported in the README, as #272 did. Otherwise leave it out and say so in the README.
- **Build.** `pnpm --filter ./packages/excel build` writes `dist/functions.js`, `dist/functions.json` (metadata for every function, with descriptions and parameter names in Vietnamese), `dist/functions.html` and `dist/manifest.xml`. The hosting base URL in the manifest comes from an env var (default `https://localhost:3000`) so users can sideload locally.
- **Docs.** Add an "Excel" section next to "Google Sheets" in README.md and README.vi.md. It shows the build command, how to sideload using Microsoft's sideloading docs, and the function table.

## Out of scope
Attaching the build to releases (release config) and publishing to AppSource. The maintainer will handle these.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `packages/excel` is `private: true` and builds the four files above
- [ ] `functions.json` lists exactly the exported functions, and a test checks that they match
- [ ] Tests in `tests/excel.test.ts` (at least 15 cases): single values, 2-D ranges, serial-number dates (for example the serial for 2026-02-17), `dd/mm/yyyy` text, and error text for bad cells
- [ ] Sheets behaviour is unchanged: `tests/sheets.test.ts` still passes
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md updated
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: The Sheets bundle reaches accountants only if they use Google Sheets. Excel is where most of them work, and the wrappers already exist.

proposals.title: sheets: add phone, name and CCCD functions (VN_SDT, VN_TACH_TEN, VN_CCCD)
proposals.body:
## Problem
The Google Sheets bundle (`packages/sheets/src/functions.ts`) covers money in words, tax IDs, lunar dates, working days and (in the full bundle) address conversion. The columns people most often clean in customer and HR sheets are phone numbers, full names and CCCD numbers, and core already handles all three: `parsePhone` (`packages/core/src/phone/index.ts`), `splitName` (`packages/core/src/name/index.ts`) and `parseCitizenId` (`packages/core/src/id/index.ts`). The bundle exposes none of them.

## Scope
Add these functions. Each accepts a single value or a range via the existing `mapRange`/`unwrap` helpers in `packages/sheets/src/shared.ts`, and returns the error text for a bad cell.

- `VN_SDT(phone, [format])`: returns `PhoneInfo.formatted` by default. With format `"e164"` it returns `e164`; with `"carrier"` it returns `carrier` (empty string if none). Add it to both bundles.
- `VN_TACH_TEN(name, part)`: part `"ho"` returns `family`, `"dem"` returns `middle`, `"ten"` returns `given`. Any other part returns an error text listing the valid values. Add it to both bundles.
- `VN_CCCD(id, [field])`: field `"hop_le"` (default) returns TRUE/FALSE for `ok`. `"tinh"` returns `province.fullName` and `"tinh_moi"` returns `newProvince.fullName` (empty string when null). `"gioi_tinh"` returns `Nam`/`Nữ` from `sex`, and `"nam_sinh"` returns `birthYear`. For a 9-digit CMND, fields other than `hop_le` return an empty string. `packages/core/src/id/index.ts` imports `address/data.js`, so put this function in the full bundle only (next to `VN_DIA_CHI_MOI` in `packages/sheets/src/address.ts` / `full.ts`), not in the lite bundle.

Write JSDoc in Vietnamese with `@customfunction`, as the existing functions do.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The three functions are exported. `VN_SDT` and `VN_TACH_TEN` are in both `vn-skills.gs` and `vn-skills-lite.gs`; `VN_CCCD` is only in `vn-skills.gs`
- [ ] The lite bundle still contains no address data, and a test asserts this
- [ ] `tests/sheets.test.ts` gains at least 12 cases: single cells, ranges, each `format`/`part`/`field` value, invalid input, and a CMND
- [ ] The README.md and README.vi.md Sheets tables list the new functions; update the bundle sizes if they change
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: Phone, name and CCCD columns are what office users clean most often, and the core functions already exist. This is a small extension of the newest distribution channel.
